Meta-cognitive AutoEvo control for residential HVAC: A cascaded physics-informed HDeePC-MPC framework with bounded self-reconfiguration
A physics-guided neural network with battery constraint mechanism for state-of-energy estimation of lithium-ion batteries
Digital twin-in-the-loop energy management for grid-edge flexibility in electrified residential buildings
Refined PEMEL operation of hydrogen-integrated islanded microgrid via penalized sensitivity region-based robust optimization
abstract: Distributed renewable generators are essential for islanded microgrids (IMGs), yet their intermittency and uncertainty may increase operating costs and induce frequency and voltage issues. Proton exchange membrane electrolyzers (PEMELs) as a controllable demand-side resource can consume surplus renewables and produce green hydrogen. However, existing PEMEL models rely on the assumption of fixed conversion rate or lack physics-grounded characterization of device-level behaviors in power grid operation. Meanwhile, conventional IMG operation focuses on keeping operating constraints and ignores robustness on objectives against uncertainties, while hydrogen demand is not treated as an explicit uncertainty source. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a refined PEMEL operation method for a hydrogen-integrated IMG via new penalized sensitivity region based robust optimization (PSRRO). First, a power-responsive PEMEL model is developed to capture nonlinear device-level characteristics driven by current density. Second, a PSRRO method is proposed to optimize IMG operation under multi-dimensional uncertainties of renewable generation, electrical load, and hydrogen demand. Lastly, an efficient solution algorithm is developed to reduce computational burdens and enhance the applicability of the PSRRO method. Numerical results verify that the proposed method can achieve robust performance by keeping both narrow objective variations and operating constraints against multi-dimensional uncertainties, with high computing efficiency for practical use.

title: Physics-informed machine learning-based adaptive predictive control for energy-efficient hybrid-cooled data centers management
A novel approach for fault location and defect quantification in large-scale photovoltaic plants
abstract: The increasing demand for renewable energy has enhanced the deployment of large photovoltaic systems. Aerial thermography is widely implemented in industry, although the accurate detection, localization, and quantification of defects still represent a major challenge for maintenance planning and performance optimization. The main contribution of this paper is a novel approach for fault location and quantification in large-scale photovoltaic plants, divided into three different phases. The first phase is the analysis of aerial parameters implemented during the monitoring procedure, e.g., GPS position, altitude, gimbal angle, etc., to define the field of view. The second phase performs thermal image processing using transformer-based deep learning models to define image-space coordinates for defect detection that will be used to extract pixel-level temperature data. Each pixel contains an associated temperature value that is analyzed using different qualitative parameters based on average temperatures, thermal load, or thermal distribution, to determine the severity of the fault. The mapping of solar plants is carried out with georeferenced visual images acquired by drones through the open-source tool OpenDroneMap, Segment Anything Model version 2, and Unidirectional Histogram. This approach is validated on two operational photovoltaic installations comprising 12 and 20 strings with 1170 and 1290 modules, respectively, achieving a module detection accuracy between 95% and 98.55%. Fault detection is performed through a RoboFlow-Detection Transformer model with an overall accuracy of 96.6%. These defects are characterized using multiple thermographic parameters, including intensity, spatial distribution, or affected area, among others, to assess their severity. The analysis of 85 detected faults reveals that 34.1% are classified as severe, 27.1% as moderate, and 38.8% as low severity. For this analysis, 12 representative cases are examined in detail, and a validation stage is conducted to assess the overall measurement process using an external infrared sensor. This procedure demonstrated an overall accuracy of ±2 °C or ± 2% of the measured value. An economic analysis to determine the feasibility of the methodology has also been developed, showing that the proposed UAV-based framework combines high diagnostic performance with a direct operational cost of approximately €202 per inspection. All these procedures confirmed the effectiveness of the proposed method in the identification of defective modules and assessing their condition through a scalable and efficient solution for maintenance in solar plants.

title: An integrated energy–carbon–economic assessment of building decarbonization at city scale
Composite phase change materials-integrated thermal management strategy for thermo-electrical coupling components dispatch
Multi-time scale operation simulation method considering extreme weather and frequency security: exploiting the multi-dimensional support capability of energy storage
Enhanced conditional diffusion modeling for probabilistic net load forecasting
Technology indicators enable early detection of decarbonization failures
abstract: Assessing decarbonization progress traditionally relies solely on tracking carbon emissions. Focusing on carbon emissions alone struggles to capture the complex uncertainties that may result in failing to identify early warning signals of decarbonization failures. Here we design and test an expanded indicator system that combines energy technology deployment with emissions to improve the early detection of long-term decarbonization failures. Using a large scenario ensemble simulated by a state-of-the-art multi-sectoral model for the US (GCAM-USA, N=2,304), we demonstrate that relying solely on the emissions indicator through 2035 is not adequate to skillfully predict decarbonization failures in 2050. In contrast, combining emissions with a range of technology indicators can substantially improve the predictive skill. This improvement is driven by the additional information provided by technological progress indicators, especially about the potential acceleration of long-term mitigation. For instance, indicators of technology deployment in early time periods can offer insights for the future potential of rapid deployment of carbon dioxide removal technologies, quick scale-up of renewable technologies, or accelerated phase-out of fossil fuels. Our study demonstrates the value of tracking technology indicators to better monitor decarbonization progress and offers insights for developing adaptive strategies to enhance the chances of decarbonization success.

title: An improved imagentime framework for hourly multi-site photovoltaic power scenario generation
Risk-aware resistance enhancement for integrated heat and power supply driven by physics-informed meteorological data
Uncertainty-aware multi-fault diagnosis in gas turbines via graph neural networks and weighted total least squares
Sustainable energy transition for BIMP regional power grid with technology ranking and optimal mix
abstract: Regional power interconnection presents an important opportunity for reaching net-zero emissions. However, technology prioritization remains challenging due to conflicting stakeholder criteria. This study develops an integrated Low Emission Analysis Platform (LEAP) and Multi Criteria Decision Analysis (MCDA) approach for technology prioritization in the interconnected grids of the Brunei-Indonesia-Malaysia-Philippines (BIMP) region. Six scenarios were developed using LEAP across six regional nodes, five interconnections and five renewable energy sources (hydro, solar PV, wind, geothermal, and biomass) for the period 2025–2050. Next, Technique for Order of Preference by Similarity to Ideal Solution (TOPSIS) analysis was performed with 11 criteria across 12 sensitivity scenarios. The results show that hydro demonstrates the most balanced profile, combining a strong multi-criteria score (0.565) with low ranking variability (mean absolute deviation/MAD of 0.611) and a 62% pairwise dominance rate. Solar PV achieves the highest multi-criteria scores (0.671) and ranks first in 8 of 12 scenarios, but its ranking drops significantly (MAD = 1.222), particularly under economic priority conditions. Optimal technology portfolios will require 77–85 GW of renewable capacity and USD 146–151 billion in investment, with a relatively balanced allocation per renewable technology. The integrated framework successfully bridges technical energy modelling with multi-criteria decision analysis, supporting the use of diversified renewable technologies rather than technology-specific strategies for regional net-zero achievement.

title: Resilient hierarchical control strategy for digital twin cloud-edge collaboration in multi-energy microgrids under non-ideal communication conditions
abstract: The wide-area coordination of Multi-Energy Microgrid (MEMG) clusters relies heavily on open communication networks. Consequently, the Cyber-Physical Systems within these clusters face severe challenges due to non-ideal communication conditions, including latency, packet loss, and noise. These impairments often compromise the convergence of traditional distributed strategies and deteriorate economic performance. To address these impediments, this paper proposes a Digital Twin (DT)-perceived cloud-edge collaborative resilient scheduling strategy for MEMG clusters. First, a communication topology adaptive reconfiguration mechanism based on Pareto optimality is established to enhance the system's structural resilience against cyber-attacks and network failures. Second, a hybrid-driven DT model, integrating a “mechanism model + residual correction network,” is constructed to achieve high-fidelity state prediction under communication constraints. These predictions serve as the initial values for the distributed consensus algorithm, thereby minimizing initial errors and mitigating aggregation bias and iterative oscillations induced by information truncation. Finally, a cloud-edge spatiotemporal decoupling mechanism is designed, employing tiered carbon pricing to guide optimal synergistic interactions between electricity and carbon across clusters. Case studies demonstrate that the proposed strategy maintains rapid and stable convergence even under severe latency and dynamic topology disturbances. Furthermore, it significantly enhances operational resilience while effectively reducing the total operating costs and carbon emissions of the clusters by up to 89.9% and 35%, respectively.

title: Planning alternatives under divergent futures: Linking transformative scenario design with bottom-up modelling and distributional impact assessment to quantify inequalities in electricity affordability
abstract: The clean energy transition promises substantial societal benefits but risks reinforcing existing inequalities if its costs and benefits are unevenly distributed. While distributional impacts have gained increasing attention in climate and energy policy analysis, many modelling frameworks remain limited in their ability to represent socioeconomic heterogeneity, bottom-up technology choices, and citizen-centred transition pathways, particularly in electricity systems with high shares of variable renewable energy. As a result, such frameworks may misrepresent electricity affordability, conceal regressive impacts, and support policy recommendations that overlook vulnerable households. This study addresses this gap by integrating bottom-up modelling with distributional impact assessment, using the Greek power sector as a case study. We develop alternative transition scenarios based on storylines informed by the concept of energy citizenship and future-world narratives. These scenarios are embedded within the OSeMOSYS modelling framework to assess alternative system-planning evolutions, costs, and emissions under conditions of heightened uncertainty and external shocks. Model outputs are subsequently combined with household budget survey data to evaluate how costs are allocated across income groups, accounting for heterogeneity in electricity consumption patterns. Our results show that decentralised, solar-oriented transition pathways could significantly improve electricity affordability compared with centralised alternatives by 2050, reducing electricity bills as a share of total income (2.4% versus 4.6%) and substantially narrowing affordability gaps between the lowest and highest income groups (6.3% versus 11%). Overall, our findings demonstrate that least-cost electricity system designs do not necessarily align with socially equitable outcomes and provide insights for designing just and inclusive energy transitions.

title: Effect of macrobubbles motion behavior on cell voltage in a zero-gap alkaline water electrolysis cell
Dynamic modeling of solar-driven adsorption subcooling CO2 booster refrigeration plant with thermal energy storage: Life cycle energy, environmental, economic insights from the world
Early-stage degradation mechanism and PINN-based state-of-health prediction of a PEMFC stack under typical ship operating conditions
Low-carbon scheduling for integrated electricity-hydrogen-gas systems with coordinated line-pack and tank-truck effects
abstract: This paper proposes a low-carbon scheduling method for integrated electricity-hydrogen-gas systems (IEHGSs) that coordinates line-pack and tank-truck effects. Firstly, a collaborative line-pack and tank-truck framework and model are developed to harness the flexibility of both stationary and mobile hydrogen storage, capturing the variable hydrogen volume fractions and dynamic storage behaviors in high-pressure gas. Then, considering the hydrogen flexibility enabled by the collaborative interaction between line-pack and tank-truck effects, a low-carbon scheduling model that incorporates uncertainties through a distributionally robust chance-constrained approach is developed, and a deterministic reformulation method is proposed to convert the objective function and constraints with random variables into deterministic form. Furthermore, a model reformulation strategy is proposed to linearize the collaborative line-pack and tank-truck effects in the intractable low-carbon scheduling model, and an iterative methodology is subsequently developed to effectively solve the reformulated model. Simulation results for IEHGSs of two different scales demonstrate that the proposed model and method significantly enhance the spatiotemporal flexibility of hydrogen storage, markedly improve the low-carbon operational performance of IEHGSs, and rapidly converge to the optimal solution while avoiding misjudgments of hydrogen volumetric fractions.

title: Integrated process design and techno-economic evaluation of electro-sustainable aviation fuel (e-SAF)
abstract: Decarbonising aviation requires large volumes of synthetic jet fuel produced from low carbon electricity and recycled CO2. This work develops and techno economically benchmarks an integrated CO2 to e-SAF process in Aspen Plus® V14, comprising four subsystems: CO2 capture, alkaline water electrolysis, RWGS-FTS fuel synthesis, and tail gas utilisation via PEMFC. At a base case, the plant converts 27.6 t/h CO2 and 3.84 t/h H2 into 5,100 kg/h of SAF, diesel and naphtha with consistent mass, carbon, and energy closure. The electricity balance is dominated by electrolyser and CO2 capture, while PEMFC credit yields only a modest net power reduction. Capital investment is strongly front loaded with CAPEX 648.6 MUSD, driven by CO2 capture (53.6%) and electrolysis (31.9%), and OPEX are electricity dominated with OPEX 140.4 MUSD/y, tightly coupling economics to renewable electricity price. Under the base financial assumptions, the discounted cash flow MFSP is 6.73 USD/kg-SAF. Sensitivity analysis of ±30%, identifies electricity price and electrolyser CAPEX as primary cost levers, followed by CO2 capture unit cost and discount rate, thereby pinpointing priority pathways for cost reduction and scale-up.

title: Dual-consensus federated electricity market coordination for privacy-preserving and democratisation-aware trading across interconnected energy communities
abstract: Interconnected energy communities require market designs that retain economic efficiency while addressing emerging needs for privacy, autonomy, and market-level democratisation. This paper proposes democratisation-aware federated multi-community electricity market (DF-MCEM) architectures for coordinating local, inter-community, and grid exchanges across heterogeneous community compositions and market designs. To operationalise objective-level democratisation, two objective components are introduced: 1) participation incentives that reward broad local engagement, and 2) an exchange channel preference index (ECPI) that prioritises local and inter-community exchange while penalising excessive grid reliance. Two privacy-preserving federated architectures are developed to embed these components into the coordination layer using SCA-ADMM: a community-level DF-MCEM (CDF-MCEM) that enforces consensus on inter-community trades, and a system-level DF-MCEM (SDF-MCEM) that introduces a second consensus on aggregated channel-usage shares. A democratic energy market index (DEMI) is introduced to evaluate realised outcomes in terms of procedural democracy, distributive equity, and spatial localism. Across nine scenarios and four architectures, activating the democratisation-aware terms increases DEMI by 0.101–0.113 absolute points relative to the non-democratised centralised benchmark. CDF-MCEM closely reproduces the democratisation-aware centralised solution, with an average welfare gap of only 0.16% and an average traded-energy gap of 0.27%. SDF-MCEM provides an explicit system-level democratisation-consensus layer, with an average welfare loss of 2.62% relative to the democratisation-aware centralised benchmark. The results show that democratisation-aware federated coordination can substantially improve participation, equity, and localism while keeping agent-level data local.

title: Robust optimization for the application strategy of medical waste plasma gasification integrated with other waste treatments
Coordinated optimal dispatch of storage-like resources based on dynamic feasible operation region aggregation
Degradation-aware design and lifetime evaluation of hydrogen hybrid marine energy systems
abstract: Hydrogen fuel cells combined with lithium-ion batteries offer a promising route to reducing emissions from short-sea shipping, but system design is complicated by discrete sizing decisions, load-dependent fuel consumption, battery buffering, and component degradation. This paper presents a degradation-aware two-stage framework for hydrogen hybrid marine energy systems. In Stage 1, a mixed-integer linear programming surrogate optimises architecture sizing and mission dispatch using an active-unit piecewise-linear representation of the nonlinear proton-exchange membrane fuel cell hydrogen-consumption map together with affine degradation proxies. A lexicographic formulation first minimises a capital expenditure-inclusive screening cost and then minimises degradation within a prescribed tolerance. In Stage 2, the optimal dispatch is post-processed using mixed-fidelity lifetime models for proton-exchange membrane fuel cell voltage loss and battery ageing, including Wang cycling fade, calendar ageing, equivalent-full-cycle tracking, and first-order Thevenin voltage evaluation. The framework is applied to a short-sea cargo-vessel retrofit comparing PEMFC/LIB and DG+PEMFC/LIB architectures across five hydrogen pathways. For PEM-electrolytic hydrogen, the selected PEMFC/LIB configuration installs five 150 kW PEMFC units and three 100 kWh battery modules, consumes 7189 kg H2 over a 194 h mission, and reduces emissions by 92.4% relative to the adopted diesel baseline. Hydrogen storage accounts for 87.0% of capital expenditure, making storage feasibility the main retrofit bottleneck. Under the adopted repeated-mission and empirical ageing assumptions, the reduced-order PEMFC health indicator reaches its voltage-loss threshold after 32 months, while battery state of health remains above 92%. Overall, the framework supports early-stage design screening by linking architecture sizing, dispatch, hydrogen pathway selection, storage requirements, and lifetime indicators within a single optimisation-evaluation workflow.

title: Heating system decarbonization decisions in homeowner associations: a Bayesian learning agent-based model
abstract: Decarbonizing shared heating systems in multi-owned apartment buildings requires collective decisions under uncertainty, in which heterogeneous households repeatedly evaluate the proposal across multiple meetings before a supermajority can pass. This paper develops a stylized agent-based framework of repeated voting in homeowner associations (HOAs / VvEs), in which households parameterized using latent-class discrete-choice estimates update beliefs about heating-system attributes through Bayesian updating with heuristic signal construction. The framework is demonstrated through a Dutch VvE setting comparing a baseline repeated-voting process with a board-mediated information architecture that combines trusted information hubs, intensified information sharing, lower hub uncertainty, and central network position. Across 100 Monte Carlo runs, the board-mediated setting reaches the 70% supermajority threshold in 70 of 100 runs versus 50 of 100 in the baseline, with mean approval rising from 63.2% to 69.0%. A component decomposition shows that the effect arises from the joint operation of the four board components rather than from any individual component. A vote-switching diagnostic based on conditional transition probabilities shows that the board-mediated architecture makes votes stickier in both directions, opponents convert less and supporters defect less, with the reduction in supporter defection robustly the larger of the two. The architecture therefore raises attainment by reducing decision volatility, with a robust supporter-stabilization component, rather than by converting entrenched opponents. The paper contributes a transparent computational framework for studying how heterogeneous preferences, belief updating, and trusted information channels jointly shape repeated collective decisions, and a testable hypothesis: a board-mediated information architecture raises supermajority attainment by reducing decision volatility and accelerating convergence, and stabilizing the pivotal, uncertainty-sensitive household class rather than converting entrenched opponents.

title: Development of switching-aware model predictive control solutions for fixed-frequency residential air conditioners
Comprehensive system level modeling of anion exchange membrane water electrolysis for high efficiency hydrogen production
Multi-objective chaos co-evolutionary optimization based on constraint-driven Q-learning for combined economic emission dispatch problems
Adaptive look-ahead economic dispatch with reinforcement learning for virtual power plant considering uncertainty
A review on thermochemical reduction of CO2 with H2 to methanol: focusing on overcoming equilibrium limitations
Techno-economic planning of battery energy storage for renewable hosting capacity in active distribution networks
abstract: This paper presents a techno-economic planning framework for battery energy storage in active distribution networks aimed at increasing renewable hosting capacity under realistic operating constraints. The problem is formulated as a bi-objective optimisation that minimises the gap to effective hosting capacity and the annualised storage cost. The cost model includes investment, operation and maintenance, and replacement cost derived from depth-of-discharge-dependent degradation computed with rainflow cycle counting over 8 760 hours. Network feasibility is checked with backward-forward sweep power flow. A two-level strategy couples the Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II with a linear-programme dispatch subproblem. Three mature battery chemistries are compared under identical conditions: lithium iron phosphate, vanadium redox flow, and lead-acid. In the MV Oberrhein benchmark, evaluated under three economic scenarios, lithium iron phosphate provides the best hosting-capacity–cost compromise. The results also show that explicit degradation changes the long-term economic ranking of the technologies. In this benchmark, the remaining hosting-capacity gain is best captured with distributed multi-site deployment rather than centralised storage.

title: Unveiling design principles for high performance dry-cathode AEMWE: Insights from 3D Multiphysics Modeling and voltage breakdown analysis
Surrogate-experiment-guided fast EIS testing method for PEMFC cold start condition via random-forest-based feature frequency extraction
Enabling large-scale underground hydrogen storage in aquifer-driven reservoirs: Integrated technology and economic feasibility
Accelerating electricity-gas energy flow analysis using global linear port model of natural gas network
Causal inference framework for smart grids with application to demand response
abstract: Smart grids generate extensive data, yet much analysis remains association-based and cannot reliably inform decisions about the effects of interventions in planning and operations. Randomized trials provide strong causal evidence but are costly and limited in scope, predictive models cannot isolate intervention effects from confounding factors, and existing causal studies in smart grids each focus on a single aspect, such as market allocation, network evolution, or temporal dependencies, without covering the complete workflow from problem formulation to decision-making. This paper introduces a domain-specific causal inference framework for smart grids that integrates established causal modeling, identification, and validation techniques into a structured workflow tailored to energy-system analysis. The framework is organized into seven phases: causal problem framing, causal model construction, data collection and preparation, causal discovery, causal inference, refutation tests and validation, and intervention evaluation and recommendation. To support adaptation across settings, the paper categorizes common causal problems in smart grids into three types (confounder-intensive, temporally structured, and real-time decision problems) and shows how the framework maps to each, with the confounder-intensive case demonstrated in detail. The framework is demonstrated through a demand response case study assessing the causal impact of pricing schemes on household electricity consumption. Using real-world data, we apply three representative causal inference methods (Backdoor Adjustment, Difference in Differences, and Double Machine Learning), benchmarked against an association-based baseline. The results show that factors influential under association can become negligible or even reverse under causal estimation, while seemingly minor factors emerge as plausible levers for decision-making under the stated identification assumptions.

title: Robust learning-enabled voltage control for water–electricity systems under incomplete topology and parameter information
Revealing the path-dependence of electro-catalyst degradation in polymer electrolyte fuel cells
DS-MS-convformer: Ultra-short-term wind power prediction based on dual-stream multi-scale convolutional transformer and hierarchical dynamic fusion
abstract: Against the backdrop of global energy transition and large-scale grid integration of wind power, ultra-short-term wind power prediction is crucial for ensuring power grid security and the efficient operation of wind farms. However, the inherent nonstationarity of wind power sequences stems from the complex coupling of time-domain transient disturbances and frequency-domain periodic fluctuations, posing two core challenges for high-precision prediction: modelling the time-frequency coupling effect and capturing multi-scale dynamic features. Existing deep learning methods often struggle to characterise this cross-scale dynamic interaction mechanism simultaneously and effectively. To address this, this study proposes a wind power prediction method based on Dual-Stream(DS) time-frequency feature decoupling modelling and hierarchical dynamic fusion. First, the technique explicitly decouples and collaboratively learns time-domain dynamic and frequency-domain periodic features through a dual-stream architecture. Furthermore, it introduces a Multi-Scale Convolutional-enhanced Transformer(MS-Convformer) that integrates local convolution and global self-attention to capture second- to minute-level turbulent fluctuations and long-period trends. Finally, through a hierarchical dynamic fusion strategy guided by a gating mechanism and cross-attention, it achieves adaptive weighting and structured integration of multi-scale features. Experimental results on real wind farm datasets show that, compared with mainstream deep learning methods, the DS-MS-Convformer method proposed in this paper achieves significantly higher prediction accuracy, providing adequate technical support for grid integration and renewable energy consumption.

title: Real-time simulation of reversible solid oxide cells for digital twins: exploration based on mechanism models and data-driven methods

A decomposition method for optimizing the operation of power-to-X energy systems with detailed process models
abstract: The growing reliance on renewable energy necessitates extending energy systems with complex processes such as power-to-X. Due to the diverse operational characteristics of these processes, the corresponding optimization problems are highly complex and result in models that are computationally difficult to solve. To address this computational challenge, this work proposes a decomposition method to solve operational optimization problems for complex energy systems with detailed process models. The method decomposes the original optimization problem into optimization problems with different levels of model granularity by incorporating a surrogate model for each process. Building on prior work focusing on a single continuous process system, this method is expanded to handle multiple and more complex process systems. To this end, we introduce a surrogate modeling approach for multistage process systems and develop three solution approaches for the operational optimization problems. The method is applied to minimize the daily operational cost of a power-to-X energy system with detailed process models of a PEM electrolyzer, a direct air capture plant and two methanation processes. All three solution approaches yield comparable operational costs, but differ in computational efficiency. The most efficient solution approach identifies an optimal operational strategy in under one hour. Additionally, a sensitivity study evaluates the impact of key parameters on the performance of the method, demonstrating its robustness and adaptability. The results highlight the potential of the proposed method to efficiently optimize the operations of complex energy systems with detailed process models.

title: Decarbonizing China's aluminium industry: a comprehensive assessment of synergistic carbon capture, utilization, and storage with renewable energy technologies
Coordinating carbon, electricity, and CCER markets for cost-effective decarbonization of China's power sector

Real-world performance and module degradation impacts of robotic cleaning in PV systems
abstract: Robotic cleaning is increasingly adopted worldwide to mitigate soiling losses in utility-scale photovoltaic (PV) systems. However, long-duration, side-by-side field evaluations of different robotic cleaning technologies under real field conditions remain scarce. This study presents the first comprehensive comparative assessment of multiple cleaning robots operating under identical field conditions in a dry and dusty desert environment. In addition to extensive outdoor and indoor experiments, a key methodological contribution of this work is the development of an irradiance-independent, short-circuit current ( Isc ) – based protocol for robust benchmarking of cleaning efficiency in outdoor environments. At the system level, the analysis considers the combined effects of robot design, module type (monofacial and bifacial), and cleaning frequency (daily, weekly, and no cleaning) to evaluate cleaning efficiency, operational reliability, electrical performance ( Pmax ), electroluminescence (EL) response, anti-reflective coating (ARC) characteristics, and module vibrations during cleaning. Results show that all robots achieved high cleaning efficiency with cleanliness restored to >99% under daily cleaning schedules, whereas extended intervals lead to residual soiling (cleanliness reduced to <95%). At module level, systematic cumulative Pmax degradation was observed in monofacial modules over time, while no consistent Pmax impact was identified across robot types. In contrast, bifacial glass–glass modules remained relatively stable. Although bifacial electrical signatures suggested reduced shunt resistance under highly penetrative robot brushes, EL, reflectivity, and surface roughness measurements were inconclusive. Module vibration under robot cleaning was minor, much less than wind-induced vibration. Overall, the results indicate that robotic cleaning could be highly effective for soiling mitigation in desert environments similar to this study site, but technology-specific validation and multi-modal diagnostics to ensure long-term module reliability prior to large-scale deployment is recommended.

title: Day-ahead and intraday coordinated IES P2P trading strategy for multi-type urban entities with bidding consensus
Adaptive energy systems planning: A rolling horizon framework with AI-enabled scenario generation
abstract: Energy systems face unprecedented challenges driven by deep uncertainty arising from evolving demand patterns, variable renewable integration, changing technology costs, and structural shifts. Building adaptive and flexible planning frameworks is becoming increasingly essential to hedge against these uncertainties, as traditional static optimization approaches that fix investment decisions in advance often struggle to adapt to rapidly evolving conditions. This paper presents an adaptive optimization framework that integrates Bayesian Neural Networks with Markov Chain Monte Carlo sampling (BNN-MCMC) for technology-specific probabilistic generation forecasting within a rolling-horizon stochastic programming formulation. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on static forecasts, the proposed methodology continuously updates scenario representations as new information becomes available, enabling investment decisions that respond more effectively to evolving system conditions. We formalize this integration through the α -BASIS framework, an adaptive extension of Bayesian Augmented Scenario Integration for Stochastic modeling, which transforms predictive distributions into probability-weighted scenarios and embeds them within a rolling-horizon stochastic programming formulation. Through an illustrative case study of the Texas energy network, we compare three planning strategies utilizing historical generation profiles of gas power plants, solar and wind farms: conventional stochastic optimization, adaptive rolling-horizon stochastic optimization, and deterministic optimization with perfect information. Results demonstrate that the adaptive rolling-horizon approach achieves total system costs only 9.7% above the perfect-information benchmark. The rolling-horizon strategy shows particular strength in incorporating updated scenario information, time-varying technology-cost trajectories, and investment timing. Overall, this work provides a practical methodology for energy planners facing deep uncertainty by bridging data-driven probabilistic forecasting with adaptive decision-making under uncertainty.

title: A systematic framework for multidimensional assessment of wake-induced performance heterogeneity in offshore wind farms
More demand, lower system costs? The flexibility value of shared autonomous electric vehicles for energy systems
abstract: Electrified transport is typically viewed as an additional source of electricity demand that increases pressure on power system infrastructure. We show that, under coordinated fleet charging, it can instead function as a large-scale demand-side flexibility resource. Unlike privately owned vehicles that must remain individually available, shared autonomous electric vehicles (SAEVs) operate as fleets in which charging can be coordinated across vehicles – and even autonomously.Using temporally resolved SAEV charging profiles, we integrate fleet charging demand into a large-scale European energy system optimisation model with endogenous investment in generation, storage, and transmission infrastructure. Scenario simulations for 2025–2040 combined with a cost–benefit analysis evaluate how SAEV deployment affects system costs, infrastructure requirements, emissions, and welfare outcomes.Our results show that coordinated fleet charging redistributes electricity demand across time and alters infrastructure requirements, generating net welfare gains despite higher electricity demand. Under medium SAEV deployment, electricity demand increases by only 4.2 TWh (0.07%) by 2040, while coordinated charging yields net social benefits of €93–140 billion in net present value. These findings highlight the importance of charging coordination for realizing the system-level benefits of electrified mobility.

title: Decarbonizing transportation with intelligent transportation systems: a systematic review of mechanisms, constraints and deployment pathways
abstract: Transportation decarbonization is increasingly constrained by the diminishing returns of conventional technological measures, prompting growing interest in Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) as a means of improving transport efficiency and sustainability. However, prior studies and reviews have largely focused on individual technologies, localized efficiency gains, or specific application scenarios, without adequately explaining whether and through what mechanisms such gains translate into net transportation decarbonization at the system level. This omission is consequential because ITS may simultaneously reduce operational emissions, reshape travel demand, shift emissions across sectors, and generate additional energy consumption through digital infrastructure. To address this gap, this paper systematically reviews the mechanisms through which ITS influences net transportation decarbonization, the constraints on its deployment, and cross-practice variation in its low-carbon effects. Drawing on a core set of 206 English-language publications identified through database searches covering 1990–2025 in the Web of Science Core Collection and IEEE Xplore and reviewed through a PRISMA-informed process, the study identifies three pathways through which ITS contributes to decarbonization: direct technological effects, structural reconfiguration effects, and adjustment and corrective effects. It further shows that ITS deployment is constrained by technical reliability, governance coordination, behavioral adoption, evaluation boundaries, and feedback capacity. Comparative case analysis indicates that technological feasibility does not necessarily ensure governance replicability. The paper develops a unified analytical framework and argues that the decarbonization value of ITS depends on whether localized efficiency gains can be translated into an identifiable, monitorable, and correctable system-level process.

title: Bi-directional charging of electric vehicles for sustainable energy management with distributed solar generation
abstract: Electrifying road transport is essential for net-zero transitions, yet large-scale residential EV charging can intensify peaks in residential low-voltage distribution networks and increase technical losses. Prior studies show that bidirectional charging (V2G) can reduce peak demand and that distributed solar generation can offset local electricity use, but these resources are often analysed separately and rarely within an integrated framework that jointly quantifies peak impacts and converter-side and network-side efficiency penalties. This study develops a peak-minimisation optimisation model that coordinates EV charging and discharging while coupling V2G with distributed solar generation, including rooftop PV and vehicle-integrated PV. The model incorporates plug-in availability, daily mobility energy requirements, state-of-charge bounds, charging/discharging power limits, UK smart-meter household demand profiles, travel-behaviour-informed EV energy needs, home-availability patterns, and the IEEE European low-voltage test feeder. Four scenarios are compared: unidirectional charging, V2G, V2G with a grid-renewable setting, and V2G with distributed solar. Results show that V2G alone reduces peak demand by 5.72% at 50% EV penetration, whereas coupling V2G with distributed solar achieves a larger reduction of 14.62% and lowers feeder I 2 R losses, despite higher conversion losses from increased energy shifting. A Monte Carlo-based uncertainty analysis further confirms that these findings remain valid under combined weather variability and stochastic EV user behaviour. Under uncertainty, the PV-aware V2G scenario achieves the lowest mean peak demand, 21.73 kW, and the largest average peak reduction, 11.58%. These findings support PV-aware coordinated charging as a practical option for peak management, feeder-loss reduction and resilient residential low-voltage energy management.

title: Load-invariant and real-time diagnostic for PEMFC via electrochemical-magnetic integration
An LLM-driven adaptive scheduling framework for fuel cell cogeneration-based integrated energy systems under source-load uncertainty
Mechanical-information-assisted state of health estimation for large-format prismatic lithium iron phosphate cells
Flexibility as a driver of regionalized power systems: A multi-regional optimization framework
abstract: In the context of the ongoing Energy Transition (ET), power system flexibility has emerged as a critical requirement for integrating increasing shares of Variable Renewable Energies (VREs) into electricity mixes. Because these resources are inherently location-specific, their large-scale deployment calls for a rethinking of how the balance between supply and demand is achieved. In this paper, we propose a multi-regional optimization framework to balance residual load using existing flexibility tools, including dispatchable generation, storage, demand response (DR), and inter-regional exchanges. Applying this framework to southern France over the full year 2022, we find that the resulting residual mix is largely low-carbon, that demand response provides substantially more downward flexibility than storage, and that inter-regional exchanges generate significant economic value. These results suggest that introducing an intermediate regional layer for the operation and coordination of power system flexibility could be beneficial from both a technical and an economic perspective.

title: An evaluation method for the node frequency support contribution of multi-type resources based on TCN-transformer-BiLSTM
Reliability-constrained stochastic sizing of a wind-powered hydrogen refueling station
Assessing building-to-grid energy efficiency and flexibility potential through bottom-up urban building energy modelling
abstract: The increasing penetration of fluctuating renewable energy sources underscores the critical role of urban building flexibility in future energy systems. However, assessing building energy efficiency and flexibility at the urban scale is challenging due to the large number and diversity of buildings in high-density urban areas. This study proposes an efficient neighbourhood-to-urban-scale Urban Building Energy Modelling (UBEM) framework to assess energy-saving and peak-shaving potentials. First, an extensive dataset of neighbourhood-scale building clusters, characterised by morphological and non-geometric attributes, was collected and processed to generate representative building-cluster archetypes. An automated workflow was then developed to convert GIS-based building cluster data into simulation-ready energy models, enabling bottom-up simulations from the neighbourhood to urban scale. Peak shaving strategies were formulated through the analysis of city-scale electricity load profiles and the application of indoor temperature setpoint adjustments. A representative case study was conducted in the core urban area of Fuzhou, China, encompassing 29,197 buildings. Results indicate that all-time setpoint adjustment strategies achieve 7–24% cooling demand savings and 2–7% electricity savings, while peak-time strategies, despite offering limited energy savings, achieve up to 25% peak load reductions with associated rebound effects. These findings highlight the potential of neighbourhood-to-urban-scale UBEM to support the scalable assessment of building-to-grid energy flexibility.

title: A diffusion-covering fusion framework for scenario generation and uncertainty representation in urban prosumer microgrids
Cold-start of high-power PEMFC stacks: inhomogeneity control and edge cell performance enhancement
A parallel distributed approach for AI-enabled online optimization of building cooling systems with enhanced efficiency, reliability and scalability
A bi-level planning model of integrated energy capacity configuration for data center cluster considering computing-electricity coupling operation and supply-demand uncertainties
Optimising national energy systems integrating heat pumps: Effects of rising cooling demand and heating demand-side management strategies
abstract: Heating and cooling interplay affects the energy system planning and operation, especially in heating-dominated countries with rising cooling demand. Heating demand-side management (DSM) measures, such as building envelope retrofit or temperature setpoint reduction can provide flexibility and facilitate HP integration, in order to avoid stress on electricity grids due to heat pumps operation. This study analyses the effect of future cooling and heating electrification in Switzerland under various DSM strategies by soft-coupling two energy system models: a physics-based building stock model (SwissRes+) and an energy optimisation model (GRIMSEL). Our results show that heating electrification has a substantial impact on capacity planning and system operation. Applying any heating DSM strategies leads to lower capacity needs and energy system costs, with retrofit showing the largest impact. Reducing thermostat setpoint (-1°C) reduces capacity investments by up to 20% or 5 GW of battery storage and levelized electricity costs by an average of 6%, therefore providing significant benefits for long-term planning. It can be considered a low-hanging fruit due to low investment requirements and potentially quick implementation. Conversely, rising cooling has a limited impact on optimal capacity planning (PV and battery storage), but affects system operation (e.g., reducing curtailments and exports while increasing self-consumption and imports), and slightly lowers levelized electricity cost, especially under higher PV adoption scenarios. These findings provide relevant insights for policymakers and energy planners to incorporate heating DSM strategies while adapting to increasing cooling demand driven by climate change.

title: A physics-guided semi-empirical degradation model for lifetime prediction of proton exchange membrane fuel cells
SOC-agnostic rapid state-of-health estimation of lithium-ion batteries
abstract: The rapid growth of retired electric vehicle batteries presents a major opportunity for low-cost stationary storage through second-life use, but current repurposing standards rely on lengthy diagnostic tests that limit through put. Fast and reliable screening methods are therefore needed to assess suitability for a second life before full recertification. This work investigates whether a short-duration (∼100s) direct-current pulse voltage response contains sufficient information for such rapid screening. We address four questions: (1) how accurately state of health (SOH) can be inferred from a short duration pulse sequence; (2) how pulse-derived features vary with state of charge (SOC) and SOH across chemistries; (3) whether physics-informed equivalent circuit model (ECM) parameters improve extrapolation across SOC; and (4) whether lightweight, SOC-agnostic models can provide practically useful accuracy and be deployed on embedded hardware. We develop a framework that extracts both statistical and physics-informed ECM features from the pulse response, characterizes their dependence on SOC and chemistry, and trains compact ElasticNet-based ensembles for LFP and NMC cells. Feature-quality analysis reveals when ECM parameters provide complementary diagnostic information and when statistical features alone suffice. Across both chemistries, we quantify the accuracy of SOH estimation under matched and mismatched SOC conditions, establishing the regimes in which cross-SOC generalization is feasible. Finally, we deploy and experimentally validate the LFP model on microcontroller based hardware, demonstrating a practical pathway for rapid, low-cost second-life battery screening that reduces reliance on traditional, multi-hour tests.

Toward high-performance vanadium-oxygen fuel cell: numerical modeling, polarization analysis, and bismuth-catalyzed anode optimization
Application-oriented unidirectional binary multi-frequency electrochemical impedance spectroscopy for lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Diagnostics for lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) in real-world applications demand fast, simple, and robust techniques. Although electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) is a powerful tool for characterising electrochemical behaviour, long measurement times and strict signal requirements limit its practical use. To overcome these challenges, this work presents a binary multi-frequency perturbation (BMFP) method that reconstructs partial EIS spectra by using a binary current excitation signal, which reduces the measurement time to just 1 5 s within the selected range of 13 frequencies from 0 . 2 H z to 2 2 4 H z . This is achieved by superimposing multiple frequency components and subsequently applying a signum function to generate a binary perturbation signal. In addition to the standard bidirectional implementation, the method also supports unidirectional current variants, either charging or discharging only. In these modes, the binary excitation is shifted by a constant current offset. This eliminates the need for a bidirectional power source, enabling compatibility with simpler charging or discharging hardware. Transient effects in the voltage response, introduced by the offset, are modelled and removed through exponential function fitting. The BMFP approach is evaluated on a total of 17 LG M50 nickel manganese cobalt oxide (NMC)-based LIBs at various ageing states, each measured across seven state of charge levels. The method achieves reconstruction errors below 2 . 2 % in impedance amplitude and 0 . 9 ⁢ ∘ in phase. To demonstrate the generalisability of the proposed method, the approach is also applied to a lithium iron phosphate (LFP)-based cell, confirming its effectiveness across different LIB types and chemistries. This work highlights the BMFP method as a fast and resource-efficient alternative to conventional EIS, paving the way for scalable, application-oriented impedance diagnostics of LIBs.

title: Green hydrogen to power scheduling in a large power grid with network constraints
abstract: Integrating green hydrogen systems into power grids introduces bidirectional and time-varying power injections that DC-based unit commitment (UC) cannot adequately address. This paper proposes an iterative decomposition framework for AC network-constrained UC with coordinated green hydrogen scheduling. The framework decomposes the problem into a master problem, formulated as a Mixed-Integer Quadratically Constrained Program (MIQCP), a subproblem that performs Newton-Raphson AC load flow analysis in DIgSILENT PowerFactory. When AC violations are detected, Sequential Convex Approximation (SCA) generates physics-informed P-cuts and Q-cuts using PTDF weighting and ∂V/∂Q sensitivities to progressively refine the master solution toward AC feasibility. The framework is validated on the modified IEEE 39-bus and IEEE 118-bus systems. A P-Q coupling cascade is identified, arising when iterative AC feasibility verification interacts with the hydrogen inventory balance. In this cascade, active power redispatch propagates through the inventory and triggers secondary voltage violations at different buses and hours. To address this, the framework includes coordinated stabilization mechanisms that prevent cut oscillation between iterations and respect the dispatch-dependent reactive capability of the hydrogen plants. On the 39-bus system, all violations are cleared within four to five SCA iterations. On the 118-bus system, the mean voltage violation count is reduced to fewer than 2 per scenario. The execution time on both systems is within the window available for day-ahead UC planning. Notably, hydrogen integration raises fuel cost on the 39-bus system but lowers total operating cost on the 118-bus system, reflecting the greater commitment flexibility of the 118-bus system relative to the 39-bus system.

title: “1 + N” mechanism and data hybrid-driven simplified modeling method for multi-unit systems and its application to multi-stack fuel cell systems
Assessing the deviation between policy and public attention in large-scale V2G deployment: evidence from multimodal data

The impact of solar photovoltaics on the energy-industry transition in the Nordic and Baltic countries
abstract: The Nordic and Baltic countries are transitioning towards net-zero energy systems relying on hydropower, bioenergy, and wind power, while rapidly falling solar photovoltaics costs are positioning it as a credible and complementary contributor. This study maps photovoltaics deployment across the region's energy system during the energy-industry transition, identifying pathways to carbon neutrality using the LUT Energy System Transition Model. Presented scenarios at country-level resolution, considering electricity exchange with Europe, examine transition speed, regional self-sufficiency, and technology cost sensitivity. The electrification-driven transition requires a four- to sixfold expansion of electricity generation capacity, with wind power and solar photovoltaics jointly supplying 79–86% of electricity in high-ambition pathways. Renewable electricity becomes the dominant source of energy, reaching 1282 TWh by 2050. Photovoltaics provides 17–22% of supply (44–54% of capacity), while wind power contributes 58–70%. The transition is characterised by declining levelised cost of electricity to 35–40 €/MWh by 2050 and levelised cost of final energy of about 46 €/MWh. A net-zero pathway by 2050 offers the most balanced outcome, maintaining renewable electricity above three-quarters of primary energy, allowing the region to develop an export potential for energy carriers, while faster defossilisation raises this cost metric to around 58 €/MWh. Energy-related CO 2 emissions decline from about 194 MtCO 2 in 2020 to net-zero between 2035 and 2050 depending on scenarios. Technology cost variations modify the technology mix but not the energy transition feasibility. Optimal combination of wind power and photovoltaics, supported by bioenergy and hydropower, ensures low-cost energy for the Nordic and Baltic countries.

title: NATTrek: A network-aware trajectory gamified visual framework for cooperative EV fleet charging under feeder constraints

Underground bio-methanation of hydrogen and carbon dioxide in depleted gas reservoirs: Thermo-hydro-bio coupled modeling
abstract: In the context of mitigating the global climate crisis and advancing the energy transition, underground bio-methanation (UBM) of H 2 and CO 2 has attracted growing attention due to its multifunctional potential in renewable energy storage and carbon utilization. However, the bio-reactive transport mechanisms involved in UBM under non-isothermal conditions remain poorly understood. To address this gap, this study develops a novel thermo-hydro-bio (THB) coupled model that incorporates multiphase multicomponent transport, heat transfer with bio-heat generation, as well as microbial growth and substrate conversion kinetics. The model is implemented using the MATLAB Reservoir Simulation Toolbox (MRST) and validated against both numerical simulations and experimental data. Based on the validated framework, the impacts of microbial kinetic parameters, geological conditions, and operational strategies on UBM performance are systematically investigated. Results indicate that the methanogen-specific growth rate plays a key role: at 4.5 × 10 −6 s −1 , conversion ratios exceeding 98% are achieved within approximately 30 days after shut-in, accompanied by an average temperature increase of over 3.3 °C. This thermal rise becomes more pronounced with increasing cycle number, leading to stronger inhibition of methanogenic activity. Lower vertical permeability, higher injection rates, and perforation at the lower part of the anticlinal axis enhance long-distance gas migration, thereby activating more methanogens and improving CO₂ conversion. Reduced production rates further enhance conversion efficiency but may compromise CH₄ recovery. Overall, this study advances the understanding of coupled THB processes in UBM and provides valuable insights for site selection and operational optimization.

title: Distribution market operators in transmission-distribution operation coordination under dual-layer uncertainty
Bridging the high-temperature gap: Co-decarbonizing industrial electricity and process heat via integrated energy systems
abstract: Industrial process heat accounts for 19% of global final energy demand, with 50% requiring high temperatures (HT) above 400°C. Yet its decarbonization pathways remain fragmented. Existing research focuses on low-temperature applications, treat electricity and heat independently, or rely on single objectives obscuring true economic and environmental trade-offs. This study develops a modular, economic and environmental multi-objective optimization framework to co-decarbonize industrial electricity and HT heat. It determines the design and dispatch of an Integrated Energy System (IES), leveraging heat electrification to maximize renewable electricity utilization. As a demonstration, it is applied to a wastewater treatment plant requiring HT process heat, integrating PV, Power-to-Heat (PtH), HT thermal energy storage (HTTES), and on-site biogas production for the case study IES. The framework evaluates location-based versus market-based (Guarantees-of-Origin) carbon accounting under policy-realistic conditions. The case study results reveal that market-based achieves higher thermal decarbonization (90.5% vs. 83.5%) at almost similar costs by oversizing the IES and utilizing shallow intra-day storage cycling. Location-based prioritizes deep multi-day storage utilization and physical self-consumption. Integrating biogas fundamentally alters the IES operational logic, achieving economic optimum in both accounting cases. Finally, a data-driven global sensitivity analysis (GSA) across 70 parameter combinations validates the framework's robustness, yielding only a ±2.7% deviation of the optimal case results and reveals that PV capital costs present 41 times greater impact on system economics than HTTES efficiency. Ultimately, this adaptable framework provides an evidence-based roadmap for policymakers, R&D funding pathways, and real time energy-intensive industries navigating their sustainable energy transitions.

title: An adaptive situation awareness model for short-term scheduling of cascade hydropower serving grids system under inflow and renewable energy uncertainties
Coordinated power regulation of clustered IBRs within grid-connected local energy communities
Estimation of hydrogen production efficiency for gas-metering-free PEM electrolyzers using broadband electrochemical impedance spectroscopy
Energy and non-energy cost-benefit assessment of motor system optimization: A review and case study–based framework
abstract: Industrial and commercial motor-driven systems account for a large share of electricity consumption and represent a major opportunity for energy savings, cost reduction, and decarbonization. However, investment decisions for motor system optimization are often based mainly on direct electricity savings, while non-energy benefits such as reduced downtime, lower maintenance costs, improved reliability, higher productivity, enhanced safety, and reduced noise are frequently omitted or treated qualitatively. This study aims to develop a structured cost–benefit evaluation framework that integrates energy benefits and non-energy benefits to support motor system optimization and investment decisions. The methodology combines a literature review, case-study synthesis, classification of motor-system optimization technologies, development of a non-energy benefit monetization index, subsector–technology weighting factors, conservative scaling factors, and sensitivity analysis. The proposed framework is applied across industrial and commercial subsectors and technologies, including premium-efficiency motors, variable speed drives, synchronous reluctance motors, and permanent-magnet motor systems. The results show that motor system optimization can deliver electricity savings, commonly exceeding 30% in applications, particularly when system-level measures such as variable speed drives and improved controls are implemented. When non-energy benefits are included under conservative assumptions, total project benefits increase substantially and estimated payback periods be reduced on average by approximately 50%, considering a large variety of case-studies. The findings demonstrate that excluding non-energy benefits can significantly underestimate the economic attractiveness of motor system optimization. The proposed framework provides decision-makers with an approach for comparing technology options, adapting benefit weights to site-specific conditions, and prioritizing investments based on combined energy, operational, financial, and environmental benefits.

title: Robust-stochastic co-optimization of wind-powered integrated energy systems capturing multi-timescale uncertainties
State of energy estimation of lithium-ion batteries based on Bayesian-optimized bidirectional temporal convolutional neural network with ECM-based feature extraction and bidirectional filtering
Long-term climate vulnerability of green ammonia economics: an integrated techno-economic and life cycle assessment across Köppen-Geiger zones
Active supercapacitor recharging strategy for electric vehicle hybrid energy storage systems under signalized interrupted traffic: preview planning and online control coordination
Structure-generalizable large models for power system operation under topology uncertainty: A graph-based foundation learning framework
abstract: This paper addresses a fundamental limitation of existing data-driven power system models, namely their inability to generalize under frequent topology changes. As modern distribution networks undergo dynamic reconfiguration due to switching operations and high penetration of distributed energy resources, models trained on fixed structures often exhibit significant performance degradation when applied to unseen configurations. To overcome this issue, we propose a structure-generalizable large model framework that reformulates power system operation as a topology-aware learning problem. The approach leverages graph-based topology encoding and multi-topology training to construct a unified latent representation space, enabling the model to capture invariant physical and operational patterns across diverse network structures. A structure-aware learning mechanism is further introduced to enhance cross-topology adaptability, while a confidence-aware prediction module quantifies uncertainty and supports reliable deployment under distribution shifts. Extensive experiments on benchmark distribution systems demonstrate that the proposed framework improves generalization accuracy by over 18.7%, reduces prediction error by 22.4%, and achieves 35.2% faster inference compared to conventional topology-specific models. These results indicate that the proposed large model paradigm provides a scalable, robust, and practical solution for real-time operation of future adaptive energy systems under inherent topology uncertainty.

title: High-frequency intraday trading for battery storages
abstract: Maximizing revenue for grid-scale battery energy storage systems in continuous intraday electricity markets requires strategies that are able to seize trading opportunities as soon as new information arrives. This paper introduces and evaluates a computationally efficient, high-frequency implementation of the rolling intrinsic trading strategy for battery energy storage systems on the intraday market for power. By combining the established rolling intrinsic logic with a full limit order book representation and a fast dynamic programming approximation, our method explicitly considers the continuously updated list of buy and sell offers, market rules, a linear approximation of degradation, and other technical parameters at a millisecond resolution. The standard rolling intrinsic strategy is adapted for continuous intraday electricity markets and solved using a dynamic programming approximation that is two to three orders of magnitude faster than an exact mixed-integer linear programming solution. A detailed backtest over a full year of German order book data demonstrates that the proposed dynamic programming formulation does not reduce trading profits and enables the policy to react to every relevant order book update, enabling realistic rapid backtesting. Our results show the significant revenue potential of high-frequency trading: our policy earns 58 % more than when re-optimizing only once every hour and 14 % more than when re-optimizing once per minute, highlighting that profits critically depend on trading speed. Furthermore, we leverage the speed of our algorithm to train a parametric extension of the rolling intrinsic, increasing yearly revenue by 8.4 % out of sample.

title: Data-driven optimization of hybrid EV charging infrastructure: From cross-city demand forecasting to dynamic allocation
PVDINO: Extracting photovoltaic panels from high-resolution remote sensing imagery via vision foundation model and dual-stream edge mining
Trustworthy digital twins for thermal and energy conversion systems: physics-grounded modeling, uncertainty-aware prediction, and operational decision support
Does energy storage abate carbon?
abstract: Energy storage can enable decarbonization by capturing surplus renewable electricity and replacing fossil-fuels during high-demand periods. Storage discharges electricity into a shared grid, where supply is delivered across sectors to meet their real-time demands, making its decarbonization benefits system-wide and time-dependent. These benefits are mediated by carbon policies that alter the generation mix, thereby shaping the carbon intensity of storage operations. The implications of storage as an indirect decarbonization enabler for electrified end-use sectors (such as transportation) are not well understood, and its system-wide decarbonization potential remains poorly quantified across sectors, carbon prices, and carbon budgets. Here, we develop the first open-source integrated assessment model tailored to Canada (representing seven regions, CAN-TIMES model), to assess decarbonization attributable to storage across 70 sub-sectors, under carbon price and budget scenarios through 2020–2050. We show that storage is particularly effective in decarbonizing sectors with pronounced daily load fluctuations, including power (22% of generation-related carbon emissions can be abated, ∼2 MtCO 2 /yr), seven transport sectors (sum as ∼1 MtCO 2 /yr, 1%), eight residential (∼2 MtCO 2 /yr, 6%), and 38 commercial sectors (∼4 MtCO 2 /yr, 12%), comparing to negligible carbon abatement in industry and agriculture. Storage's system-wide carbon abatement cost rises from 9 to 22 to 57–121 CAD/tCO 2 between 2021 and 2050, remaining broadly below Canada's federal carbon-price trajectory. Storage capacity can expand under higher carbon prices or tighter carbon budgets as arbitrage value improves, but its marginal abatement potential can decline as the system approaches full decarbonization.

title: A bottom-up energy-economic-environmental-reliability optimization framework for hybrid renewable energy systems in near-zero energy buildings under dynamic load conditions
Turning current mismatch into advantage: suppressing hysteresis and improving operational stability in two-terminal perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells
abstract: Under real-world operation, solar cells can be subject to unstable and unpredictable operating conditions, including variations in illumination levels and swings in operating voltages. This poses a challenge to the viability of perovskite-based solar cells (PSCs), where it is becoming increasingly well understood that operating conditions other than fixed MPP bias can accelerate ageing, such as through ionic cycling or exposure to reverse bias. In this contribution, we illustrate how these critical real-world stresses can be substantially avoided through deliberate mismatch of the subcell photocurrents in a series-connected silicon-perovskite tandem solar cell. When the non-perovskite cell limits tandem photocurrent, the perovskite subcell voltage is more stable and predictable under variations in the tandem cell voltage. This suppresses hysteresis and stabilizes tandem power output by mitigating voltage-cycling-induced fatigue and performance loss. Conversely, there is significant disadvantage to a perovskite current limited configuration, where hysteresis and instability can be enhanced, and the perovskite subcell can be pushed into reverse bias under increasingly large positive bias of the tandem cell. Current mismatch requires a minor performance trade-off, but we show that a power loss of less than ∼5% rel. is sufficient to produce measurable improvements in power output stability.

title: Negative externalities of imported electricity in interconnected power network: mechanism analysis and internalization approach
Integration of photovoltaic energy storage system (PV-ESS) with in-motion charging infrastructure planning and scheduling for e-buses
A DSSR-based observation approach for distribution systems
Confidence-driven resilient energy management of offshore wave-powered DC microgrids with non-collocated storage under complex sea states
Spatio-temporal heterogeneous graph-based modeling and temperature prediction for data center indoor system
Toward intelligent and resilient green hydrogen production: Digital twin technologies for AWE, AEM, PEMWE, and SOEC electrolysis systems and future perspectives
Causal inference multi-agent reinforcement learning for energy-efficient HVAC control in multi-zone buildings
Electricity market reform proposals through the lens of the energy trilemma: A state-of-the-art review
abstract: The accelerating transition toward decarbonized electricity systems is challenging the adequacy of traditional market designs to deliver reliable, affordable, and sustainable energy. This paper presents a comprehensive, state-of-the-art review of electricity market reform proposals, systematically analysing their capacity to address the energy trilemma: affordability, security of supply, and environmental sustainability. Drawing on a PRISMA-based literature review of 263 peer-reviewed studies (2010–2025), the analysis synthesizes reform options across three key dimensions: price formation mechanisms, system flexibility and reliability, and integration of renewable energy sources. The review evaluates a range of market design innovations, including adjustments to auction formats, capacity remuneration mechanisms, demand-side management, and long-term contracting frameworks, highlighting their empirical effectiveness, implementation challenges, and context-dependent trade-offs. The evidence base is predominantly European and U.S., with targeted references to major emerging economies (China, India, Brazil, South Africa). We find no universal design. Tailored portfolios of incremental and structural changes are required. We conclude with research gaps and policy priorities.

title: A reliability-guided supervision and trajectory learning framework for health monitoring and Long-term prognostics of electric vehicle battery packs from field data
Coordinated scheduling of a hydro-PV-hybrid energy storage system considering operational safety constraints and lifetime degradation
A novel yawed wake model capturing full-wake heterogeneity with application to layout-yaw co-optimization in utility-scale wind farms
Dual-mode resilient dispatch for V2G systems with PBT-enhanced multi-agent deep reinforcement learning
Optimizing the configuration and capacity of flexibility retrofits in multiple power plants using a bi-level optimization approach
Counterfactual load forecasting with LLM-structured events and representation learning
abstract: News-reported social, environmental, and grid events can substantially reshape electricity demand, yet quantifying how such events perturb forecasted load trajectories remains largely unaddressed. Existing news-augmented forecasting studies use news as auxiliary features to reduce prediction error but cannot answer counterfactual questions about demand under alternative event conditions. Counterfactual forecasting naturally formulates this problem by comparing the factual trajectory under observed news with counterfactual trajectories under alternative treatments, such as removing events or injecting hypothetical scenarios. However, counterfactual outcomes are inherently unobservable, so the prediction error cannot be directly minimized from data. This challenge is compounded by confounding: news occurrence is entangled with weather, calendar, and historical load conditions that independently affect demand. Guided by a generalization bound for continuous treatments that decomposes the unobservable counterfactual error into weighted factual loss and representation balance, this paper proposes the News-Aware Counterfactual Load Analysis Framework (NACF) to control this error upper bound through observable training objectives. NACF converts unstructured news into structured event streams via an offline large language model, encodes these as continuous semantic treatments with a no-news baseline, and estimates treatment-dependent load trajectories through a varying-coefficient response network with learned sample reweighting and Integral Probability Metric (IPM)-based representation balance regularization. Experiments on an Australian electricity-demand dataset show that NACF remains competitive in factual forecasting while providing evidence of treatment-intensity structure, improved representation balance, and interpretable demand perturbations in synthetic interventions and real event case studies.

title: Constraint learning-based optimal operation of district cooling systems with distributed water thermal energy storage
Understanding global social acceptance of hydrogen technologies: trust, adoption barriers, and policy insights from an international survey
abstract: Hydrogen is increasingly recognized as a key energy carrier with potential to support energy security and climate mitigation. While techno-economic and environmental aspects are well studied, the social dimension of hydrogen deployment remains comparatively underexplored. This study addresses this gap through an international survey of more than 1000 respondents, providing global insights into the factors shaping public acceptance of hydrogen technologies. The survey covers demographic characteristics, general awareness, and perceptions of specific hydrogen applications. The results show that universities and research centers are the most trusted sources of information, emphasizing the critical role of scientific institutions in shaping public understanding. Hydrogen technologies are generally perceived as safe; however, acceptance is strongly influenced by access to reliable information and public awareness. Economic factors emerge as a key driver, with respondents indicating that financial incentives would significantly increase adoption willingness. Applications such as hydrogen use as a chemical feedstock and for renewable energy storage are viewed most favorably, reflecting their higher technological maturity and policy support. Overall, the findings demonstrate that trust and economic considerations, rather than safety concerns, are the main determinants of hydrogen acceptance. This highlights the need to integrate social-perception indicators into energy planning and to align hydrogen policies with effective communication strategies and targeted economic support.

title: Economy-oriented resilient tube-based MPC for load frequency control of gas-electricity coupling systems under wind uncertainty and DoS attacks
A pattern-based heliostat field layout generation method with gradient-weighted azimuthal compression and inter-row optical avoidance
Distributionally robust capacity optimization for hydrogen-based multi-energy systems: Integrating chain-wide energy conversion characteristics under variable operating conditions
Atomically engineered hierarchical porous biomass carbon: from multiscale design to advanced energy storage and fundamentals
An online safety-aware deep reinforcement learning-based method for flexible support of distributed energy resources in distribution networks
Physics-aware visual prompting for ultra-short-term photovoltaic forecasting: A multimodal fusion method based on satellite imagery
Driving condition feature driven collaborative energy conversion and management strategy for electric commercial vehicles with the dual-motor coupled powertrain system
Imbalance-robust retired battery sorting via semi-supervised contrastive representation learning
abstract: Effective sorting of retired lithium-ion batteries is a prerequisite for safe and reliable second-life deployment, yet it remains challenging in practice due to heterogeneous degradation behaviours, limited labels, and pronounced class imbalance.
