To achieve imbalance-robust sorting, this paper proposes a semi-supervised contrastive representation learning framework built upon a unified Visual Geometry Group 16-layer network (VGG16). Specifically, state of charge–discharge voltage curves are transformed into pseudo-colour images and processed by a pre-trained VGG16 backbone for efficient end-to-end feature extraction. To reduce redundancy and highlight discriminative information, convolutional feature responses are further exploited to identify discharge segments exhibiting the most prominent inter-class differences, which are then used as the key inputs for subsequent learning. On this basis, a semi-supervised contrastive objective is introduced to improve intra-class compactness and enlarge inter-class separability, with particular emphasis on strengthening minority-class representations under imbalanced data. Experiments on the public dataset and our private dataset validate the effectiveness of the proposed method, achieving 94.34% accuracy and 0.942 F1-score on the public dataset, and 95.35% accuracy and 0.924 F1-score on the private dataset, respectively. These results suggest that the proposed framework can support fast and reliable retired-battery sorting through a rapid test procedure, thereby reducing sorting uncertainty and safety risks, improving pack consistency for second-life assembly, and facilitating scalable and cost-effective battery reuse.

title: An air-cooled PEMFC with closed-cathode air intake design: independent cathode airflow regulation to achieve better output performance, environmental adaptability and durability
Demand affordability-concerned resilience planning under investment cost uncertainties
Sustainable energy management for hybrid electric ships: Multi-energy architectures, lifecycle degradation, MVDC stability, and deployment pathways
Phase-change-material-enhanced thermal management for stable solar hydrogen production: Mechanism and operational behaviour
Joint optimization of electric bus operation and battery charging considering renewable microgrid interactions
Cultural heritage as a structural modifier of rooftop solar deployment: A building-level framework for heritage-constrained urban decarbonisation
abstract: Cultural heritage protection constrains rooftop photovoltaic (PV) deployment across a substantial share of the European building stock, yet existing solar cadastres consistently ignore heritage-related regulatory constraints, leading to systematic overestimation of deployable PV capacity in historically developed urban environments. This study develops and applies a heritage-aware analytical framework that integrates building-level energy-demand modelling, a GIS-based rooftop PV cadastre and scenario-based interpretation of heritage regulations to assess realistic decarbonisation pathways for heritage-constrained urban building stocks.Applied to the Municipality of Maribor, Slovenia, the framework shows that formally protected buildings account for a disproportionately large share of technically suitable rooftop area — more than three times their share of the building stock. Across five heritage-based scenarios, deployable rooftop PV potential ranges from 68% to 93% of the technical baseline, with differences determined primarily by institutional interpretation of regulations rather than the legal framework itself. Heritage constraints produce differentiated building-level electricity self-sufficiency outcomes, with residential and public-sector buildings in heritage-sensitive areas most affected under restrictive regulatory interpretations.At the municipal scale, rooftop PV alone cannot achieve electricity self-sufficiency under deep electrification pathways toward 2050, and a substantial residual electricity gap persists across all scenarios. A critical finding is that deeper building renovation without corresponding relaxation of PV admissibility rules widens rather than narrows this gap — demonstrating that renovation depth and PV admissibility must be treated as complementary policy levers rather than independent instruments. Heritage protection therefore acts as a structural modifier rather than a binary barrier to urban PV deployment, simultaneously constraining on-site renewable generation and limiting achievable renovation depth.The proposed framework provides a transferable, applied tool for more realistic assessment of deployable solar potential and decarbonisation pathways in heritage-constrained urban environments, directly supporting the integration of heritage constraints into urban energy planning, solar cadastre design and national building renovation strategies across European municipalities.

title: Embedded efficiency surrogate model-based day-ahead joint bidding for energy and frequency regulation of vanadium redox flow batteries
Cantilevered piezoelectric energy harvesting for road transportation energy systems: From vibration-structure coupling to circuit adaptation and field deployment
Risk-aware pre-deployment, information-quality-driven defense, and stage-coupled recovery for airport integrated energy systems against multi-type cyberattacks
The significance of a polarization curve - analysis of a 60-cell polymer electrolyte water electrolysis stack
abstract: The objective of this study is to demonstrate the diversity of information encapsulated within a polarization curve and its operational boundary conditions. To this end, a polymer electrolyte membrane water electrolysis stack comprising 60 cells with an active cell area of 1024 cm2 has been constructed and characterized. The performance data such as the average cell voltage of 1.88 V at the maximum applied current density of 3 A cm−2 and a minimum specific power requirement of 4.01 kW h m−3N,H2 hydrogen at standard conditions at partial load (0.6 A cm−2) were extracted from the polarization curve. In addition, the current-dependent single cell voltage distributions, the pressure and temperature differences for the anode and cathode side could be determined, as well as the Faraday and voltage efficiency. The maximum Faraday efficiency recorded was 97.6 %, and the voltage efficiency was 84.8 %LHV. A significant finding was the measurement of an H2 in O2 concentration of 0.44 %vol at 0.02 A cm−2 which is way below the critical concentration of 4 %vol. Stack parameters and the begin-of-life state are determined based on the polarization curve and the supporting sensors.

title: Hierarchical coordination optimization for grid-interactive hybrid energy systems with hydrogen and battery storage
Can Italy decarbonise without raising bills? A scenario-based assessment of renewable, flexibility and adequacy policies on power system costs through 2035
abstract: This paper assesses the potential evolution of the Italian electricity market under two alternative policy configurations: long-term Contracts for Difference (CfD), reflecting recent reforms, and pure merchant investment under the System Marginal Pricing (SMP) regime. Motivated by recent energy price volatility and investment uncertainty, we investigate whether Italy’s policy shift can achieve key objectives: supporting decarbonisation, enhancing energy security and ensuring affordability. We employ the NET model — a system-dynamics framework calibrated on national data and policy targets — extended to incorporate CfD auctions, the MACSE storage-procurement mechanism, capacity-remuneration tools and Terna’s planned grid upgrades. Using 12-year Monte Carlo simulations (2024–2035), we compare outcomes in terms of renewable energy deployment, system-cost efficiency and consumer-price dynamics, and test robustness via sensitivity analyses. Our results demonstrate that renewables reduce consumer bills and narrow future price volatility, yet neither CfD nor SMP alone meets the National Energy and Climate Plan’s 2030 decarbonisation target — a shortfall driven by low ceiling prices in CfD auctions and moderate fossil-fuel price forecasts under SMP. While electricity price differences between the two market designs remain modest, beyond a certain RES penetration threshold, CfD is more effective at containing price spikes, whereas SMP facilitates faster long-term price declines via accelerated RES investment. These findings imply that policymakers should periodically recalibrate CfD auction parameters — particularly ceiling prices — to maintain alignment with evolving market conditions. Conversely, relying solely on merchant initiatives risks subjecting policy targets to uncontrolled fossil-fuel price fluctuations.

title: Pre-trip energy consumption prediction for battery electric vehicles via long-tail-aware cost-sensitive ensemble learning
Reducing energy not supplied in islanded operation mode of microgrids via optimal load prioritization in distribution expansion planning
A computationally efficient physics-based equivalent circuit model for real-time simulation of electrochemical-thermal behavior in lithium-ion batteries
A solar distributed low-carbon energy system for urban buildings: design and multi-objective optimization for favorable 3E performance
Assessment of microbial hydrogen technologies over the last decade: is it a future-ready technology?
A self-supervised constraint-embedded neural network for AC optimal power flow
abstract: Alternating Current Optimal Power Flow (AC-OPF) is a fundamental but computationally demanding problem in power system operation. Recent neural-network-based optimal power flow (OPF) methods have been developed to reduce online computation time relative to iterative optimisation solvers. Within this literature, feasibility has been improved relative to unconstrained direct neural prediction by incorporating physics-informed training, warm-starting, feasibility restoration, or constraint-aware loss functions. However, many existing approaches still rely on pre-solved OPF solutions, fixed or manually tuned penalty terms, solver-based refinement, data-synthesis pipelines, or formulations that do not directly address label-optional learning for the full nonlinear and nonconvex AC-OPF problem. This paper introduces SCENE-OPF, a self-supervised, constraint-embedded neural network framework for solving the full nonlinear and nonconvex AC-OPF problem. Here, self-supervised refers to deriving the training signal from the AC-OPF objective and physical constraints, rather than relying exclusively on solver-generated labels. Historical OPF solutions, when available, can be incorporated as auxiliary supervision, but they are not required by the constraint-embedded training objective. By incorporating the Exterior Penalty Augmented Lagrangian Method (EPALM) with adaptive multiplier updates into neural network training, the proposed framework embeds the OPF objective, equality constraints, and inequality constraints directly into the learning process. Evaluations on IEEE standard test cases of increasing size show that SCENE-OPF maintains strong constraint satisfaction and competitive solution accuracy across the tested systems, with particularly improved feasibility relative to representative neural OPF baselines in the larger tested cases. Sensitivity analysis further shows that removing historical OPF labels mainly affects early-stage convergence, while comparable final feasibility and optimality can still be achieved under the tested settings. Transfer-learning experiments also indicate that SCENE-OPF can adapt to unseen load scenarios within the same network with faster convergence.

title: Huber-CVaR-based distributionally robust bilevel optimization for energy hubs integrating heterogeneous flexibility resources
abstract: As a core unit for multi-energy coupling and conversion, energy hubs (EHs) face key challenges, including incomplete modeling of emerging flexible resources, limited approaches for uncertainty management, and insufficient multi-agent game mechanisms. To address these issues, this paper proposes a distributionally robust bilevel optimization method for EHs that integrates heterogeneous flexibility resources. First, an EH model is developed that incorporates diverse flexible elements such as data centers, electric vehicles, electrolyzer systems, and multi-energy loads. Second, a novel distributionally robust optimization (DRO) method is proposed, integrating the Huber ambiguity set with conditional value-at-risk (CVaR). It leverages the smooth differentiability and outlier robustness of the Huber loss function along with the tail-risk control capability of CVaR. Furthermore, considering the heterogeneous and multi-agent nature of EH systems, a unified framework is formulated by integrating the Huber-CVaR DRO with a bilevel leader-follower model, enhancing collaborative decision-making under uncertainty. Then, to tackle the model reformulation and computational complexity, an efficient solution strategy is designed based on the KKT conditions, strong duality, type-1 special ordered sets (SOS1), and a tailored column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm. Finally, case studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed model and methodology.

title: Resilience quantification and enhancement of typhoon-affected distribution system with virtual power plant
abstract: Rising incidents of extreme weather events and the increasing penetration of stochastic distributed energy resources have led to critical research on enhancing power system resilience in recent years. Strengthening resilience against high-impact, low-frequency events requires quantifying a given system’s resilience and integrating this quantification into the energy management model of the power system. This paper proposes a unified resilience metric that accounts for the impact of extreme weather on various technical and economic parameters of power system operation, enabling a comprehensive assessment of power system resilience. In addition, a novel virtual power plant (VPP) scheduling framework is developed that incorporates two operational resilience enhancement strategies, distribution network reconfiguration and demand response programs, to improve distribution system performance during extreme events while simultaneously optimizing operation under normal conditions. The effectiveness and advantages of the proposed resilience metrics and VPP scheduling framework are validated through simulation and comparative analyses on a 33-bus distribution network integrated with electric vehicle charging stations, battery swapping stations, solar generating units, and flexible loads at multiple bus locations. The results demonstrate a substantial improvement in system resilience, as reflected by a 96% reduction in the value of the proposed unified resilience metric and a 35% improvement in the system’s load-serving capability.

title: Cooperative bid and operation strategy in two-settlement energy market through dual-agent imitation learning on joint optimized policy
abstract: This study proposes a reinforcement learning (RL)-based bidding and operation model for solar energy storage systems, designed to maximize electricity market profits under operational uncertainty. The model introduces a cooperative dual-agent framework within a market environment structured around a two-settlement market mechanism, employing offline learning and cooperative strategy development. To jointly derive optimal bidding and operation strategies, the problem is reformulated as a decentralized partially observable Markov decision process (Dec-POMDP), and a centralized training with decentralized execution (CTDE) architecture is adopted to enable collaborative decision-making between the bidding and battery operation agents. Notably, the proposed offline RL framework learns joint policies by imitating optimal decisions derived under perfect foresight of future market conditions, using an optimized joint policy demonstration (OJPD) approach. Experimental results show that the dual-agent structure outperforms traditional single-agent RL methods in profitability. Furthermore, integrating CTDE significantly enhances performance, and training with joint policy demonstrations based on perfect market foresight not only improves profitability but also ensures stable and consistent bidding and operation decisions.

title: Planning highway charging networks for heavy-duty electric vehicles: From network design to station-level charging profiles
abstract: As freight electrification progresses, the planning of high-power charging infrastructure becomes a critical challenge due to the interaction between time-constrained operations, spatially uneven demand, and limited grid-connection capacity. Current European Union regulation specifies corridor coverage requirements, but does not explicitly account for local demand intensity, station sizing, or grid constraints. This article presents an integrated optimization framework for planning highway charging infrastructure for heavy-duty electric vehicles (HDEVs). The framework combines freight-tour simulation, route- and energy-aware charging event generation, candidate-site identification, and optimization-based station siting, sizing, and event-level scheduling. In addition, a constant-current/constant-voltage (CC–CV) post-processing step is used to obtain more realistic charging durations and aggregate charging profiles. The framework is applied to the Netherlands for 2025, 2030, and 2040 under both demand-driven and regulatory-driven planning paradigms, considering charger ratings of 350 kW and 1 MW. The results show that demand-driven planning achieves full event feasibility on the modelled corridor network, whereas the regulatory-driven planning exhibits a small but persistent feasibility gap due to its more geographically constrained candidate set. Across scenario years, infrastructure expansion follows a two stage pattern, shifting from initial spatial coverage to capacity densification at persistent freight corridors. Sensitivity analysis further shows that 1 MW networks are substantially more exposed than 350 kW networks to grid limits and vehicle-side charging assumptions. Overall, the proposed framework provides a practical decision support tool for designing scalable, cost-effective, and operationally realistic HDEVs charging networks.

title: Bi-timescale distributionally robust optimization for power-computing-carbon coordination in multi-microgrids with data centers
Reconfiguring flexibility in renewable power-to-ammonia systems using molten-salt thermal energy storage in the ammonia synthesis loop: A coordinated electro‑hydrogen-thermal scheduling approach
abstract: In renewable power-to-ammonia (ReP2A) systems, the intermittency of wind and solar generation propagates through electrolytic hydrogen production and induces thermal instability in the ammonia synthesis reactor (ASR). The resulting temperature cycling accelerates fatigue and shortens service life, while reactor thermal inertia limits flexible start-up, shutdown, and load adjustment. To address this issue, this study integrates molten-salt thermal energy storage (MS-TES) into the Haber-Bosch synthesis loop and develops a coordinated electro-hydrogen-thermal scheduling framework. MS-TES decouples hydrogen supply fluctuations from reactor thermal dynamics by enabling hot standby operation and sustained thermal support during start-up and low-load conditions. A state-space model is established to capture the thermal dynamics of the ASR and MS-TES. Based on this model, an optimal scheduling program coordinates ammonia synthesis operation with hydrogen production, battery energy storage (BES), and hydrogen storage (HS). The problem is formulated as a mixed-integer linear program (MILP) and extended with information gap decision theory (IGDT) to address renewable uncertainty. Case studies based on an industrial-scale project in northern China show that MS-TES enhances reactor thermal stability and system-level flexibility, while diminishing the marginal benefit of large BES capacity. As a result, a configuration combining small BES, HS, and MS-TES achieves near-equivalent performance to large-BES systems, with lower investment and improved economic returns. Year-round simulations further show that MS-TES avoids ASR start-up and shutdown and delivers consistently higher net revenue under variable renewable conditions.

title: Long-term deployment of marine current turbines: a review of biofouling effects on performance degradation, mitigation strategies and techno-economic impacts
abstract: Marine current turbines (MCTs) are a promising technology for predictable renewable energy generation, but their long-term performance is significantly affected by the harsh marine environment. Among the various degradation mechanisms, biofouling is one of the most critical, as it increases surface roughness, modifies hydrodynamic loads, reduces energy conversion efficiency, and raises operation and maintenance costs. This review critically examines the effects of biofouling on MCT performance by integrating hydrodynamic, biological, operational, and techno-economic perspectives. Existing experimental, numerical, and field studies indicate that moderate biofouling typically reduces the power coefficient by 10–20%, while severe natural colonisation may lead to power losses exceeding 40%, with the magnitude of degradation depending on fouling morphology, turbine configuration, installation conditions, and operating strategy. The effectiveness and limitations of current mitigation approaches, including antifouling and foul-release coatings, adaptive tip-speed-ratio control, cleaning schedules, and component-specific maintenance strategies, are systematically discussed. A key contribution of this review is the identification of the gap between site-specific biofouling observations, predictive growth modelling, and turbine performance assessment. To address this limitation, an integrated framework is proposed that combines local biofouling monitoring, hydrodynamic modelling, and techno-economic indicators to support lifecycle performance assessment. The analysis highlights that biofouling should be considered not only as a surface degradation phenomenon but also as a key lifecycle driver influencing turbine design, maintenance planning, annual energy production, and the economic viability of tidal energy systems.

title: EVaR-based risk-aware scheduling strategy for port integrated multi-energy systems under extreme weather conditions
Label-free conditional synthesis of load and renewable generation profiles via unsupervised latent disentanglement
Reframing Data Centers as Strategic Producers: Energy-Data Nexus
Safe reinforcement learning-based robust scheduling for energy systems: Experimental validation and energy management insights
STD-MoE: Structured time-series decomposition with sparse mixture-of-experts for photovoltaic power uncertainty forecasting
Benders-based solution strategies for stochastic capacity expansion models with loss of load probability constraints
abstract: As variable renewable energy and storage expand, assessing and planning for resource adequacy (RA) in power systems is becoming more critical. Nevertheless, capacity expansion models (CEMs) typically rely on deterministic reserve margin constraints that only crudely approximate RA, so that detailed ex-post RA simulations are needed to verify that the CEM solution is sufficiently reliable. In this paper, we formulate a two-stage stochastic CEM that directly incorporates a loss-of-load probability (LOLP) RA requirement via a chance constraint. This large problem is challenging to solve, so we implement a scenario-wise Benders decomposition (BD) algorithm and fortify it with two structure-aware strategies. Both rely on a pre-processing step that ranks scenarios by their scenario intensity factor (SIF), a metric that approximately reflects how difficult it is to meet loads in each scenario. Using the SIF ranking, we enhance Benders with stronger initial feasibility cuts (BD+Cuts), guided scenario reduction (BD+SR), and both these strategies combined (BD+Cuts+SR). In a Texas-inspired case study featuring multiple zones and hundreds to thousands of scenarios, our BD-based algorithms succeed in quickly obtaining optimal solutions where an off-the-shelf solver fails to converge. Our Cuts and SR strategies individually reduce solve times substantially relative to BD alone, especially as the number of zones grows (mainly due to Cuts), and their combination accelerates convergence by up to 90%. Our CEM-LOLP formulation and efficient algorithms allow us to compute and visualize the tradeoff between the LOLP target and total cost, demonstrating the value of our approach for informing power system planning decisions.

title: Frost-suppression resilience of a novel unglazed solar-air dual-source heat pump system: a multi-climatic study
Fault diagnosis of lithium-ion batteries using dynamic multi-time-scale decomposition of relaxation behavior
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely used in electric vehicles (EVs) and energy storage systems (ESSs) because of their high energy density and reliable performance. However, aging and manufacturing defects can compromise safety, efficiency, and lifetime, highlighting the need for early fault diagnosis in battery management systems (BMSs). Conventional state-evaluation methods based on pulse-derived direct-current internal resistance (DCIR) show substantial overlap between normal cells and those with electrode misalignment defects, limiting single-threshold early detection. To address this limitation, this study proposes an early anomaly detection framework that exploits voltage relaxation behavior following pulse currents during fast charging, using an SOC-windowed charge–rest protocol. Relaxation voltage time series are transformed into image snapshots via time-delay embedding and Hankel–Gramian Angular Field (GAF) mapping to better capture system dynamics. Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD) decomposes the response into dominant temporal and spatial modes across multiple time scales. Texture features are extracted from spatial-mode images using Local Binary Pattern (LBP) histograms and statistical descriptors, then projected into a PCA-based latent space constructed exclusively from normal-cell data. Hotelling's T 2 , Q statistics, and a combined fault score are used for anomaly assessment, with performance evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Results show limited detection at low SOC (30–35%) due to phase-transition effects, whereas robust detection is achieved at 40–55% SOC, with accuracy, precision, recall, and F1-score consistently above 0.9. Requiring only voltage–current data and short rest periods, the proposed method demonstrates the feasibility of a practical, sensor-free approach for early detection of electrode misalignment defects under controlled charging–relaxation conditions.

title: Vertical mounted bifacial PV deployment in cities to reduce supply-demand mismatch with increased revenue
Agrivoltaics could increase global land use efficiency compared to bioenergy
abstract: Climate change mitigation scenarios often include a substantial bioenergy component, raising concerns about the land use impacts of large-scale energy crop production. However, agrivoltaic systems have the potential to generate electricity with a higher land use efficiency than bioenergy by integrating photovoltaic panels into agricultural land. Here, we model the global land system to explore the land use impacts of energy crops, agrivoltaics, and photovoltaics under a 1.5°C climate change mitigation scenario. Bioenergy demand in the bioenergy scenario increases almost six-fold from 2020 to 2060. Replacing all bioenergy with agrivoltaics requires 30 times less land, leading to 106 Mha more natural land cover, 52 Mt less nitrogen fertiliser applied, and 305 km3 less irrigation water withdrawn per year by 2060. Similar but smaller reductions in land use are achieved with standard photovoltaic systems. Our findings suggest that future net cropland expansion can be avoided by prioritising agrivoltaic and photovoltaic systems over bioenergy. Policies that incentivise the adoption of agrivoltaics could increase global land use efficiency, reducing the trade-offs between energy supply, food production, and nature protection.

title: ECLAR-Net: An expert-guided contrastive learning and adaptive reasoning network for robust electricity theft detection
Risk-aware day-ahead baseline scheduling and real-time rolling correction for coupled EV charging and edge-service operation under distribution-network constraints
Breaking the data scarcity barrier in HVAC fault diagnosis via feature-sample collaborative augmentation
abstract: Data-driven heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) fault detection and diagnosis (FDD) plays a vital role in enhancing building energy efficiency; however, the extreme scarcity of real-world fault samples hinders model training and remains the primary bottleneck to practical implementation. Current research largely relies on sample-level oversampling or generative augmentation, which struggles to produce stable and informative data under limited-sample conditions. Meanwhile, feature-level enhancement remains underexplored, which limits the deeper representation of fault mechanisms. To overcome these limitations, this study proposes a feature–sample collaborative augmentation (FSCA) framework that integrates feature enhancement with sample augmentation in a unified manner, thereby enlarging the effective learning space and extracting the maximum value from limited datasets. On the feature side, a spatially correlated feature mapping-based enhancement method is proposed to achieve continuous mapping from correlation modeling to spatial visualization, yielding more discriminative feature representations. On the sample side, a stable augmentation strategy based on an improved denoising diffusion probabilistic model is proposed, incorporating conditional generation and squeeze–excitation attention to enhance the stability, controllability, and fidelity of generated samples. Experimental results demonstrate that FSCA significantly improves FDD accuracy under severe sample scarcity, achieving performance gains of up to 8.63% and 15.18% on two building HVAC systems, and clearly surpassing state-of-the-art methods. These findings highlight the effectiveness and application prospects of FSCA for HVAC FDD, providing a promising solution for data-driven FDD deployment in real-world small-sample environments.

title: A GIS-MCDA method for renewable energy prosumer integration in road construction compound siting: development, demonstration, and evaluation
abstract: The global transition to renewable energy (RE) is essential for sustainable development and climate change mitigation. However, integrating RE into road construction remains largely overlooked in both research and practice. Construction compounds—operational hubs for road projects, are energy-intensive; yet their siting is typically based on logistics, cost, and regulatory considerations, with minimal attention to onsite RE potential. This study develops, demonstrates, and evaluates a Geographic Information Systems-Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis (GIS-MCDA) method to identify optimal construction compound locations supporting RE prosumption, using Uganda's Busega–Mpigi Expressway as a case study. The method integrates constraint mapping with solar and wind suitability modelling using Weighted Linear Combination (WLC). Wind conditions (0.1–3.8 m/s; <4 m/s threshold) were infeasible, while solar analysis identified four priority construction compound locations (PCC1–PCC4), with PCC3 performing best, reflecting a distribution of 75% low, 21% moderate, and 4% high suitability classes. Sensitivity analysis confirmed robust spatial rankings across alternative weighting scenarios. Comparison with the existing compound revealed a recoverable energy gap of 8.3%, increasing annual output by ∼120 MWh, yielding USD 42,000–48,000 savings and ∼ 84 tCO₂/year avoided emissions. Stakeholder evaluation using the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) showed strong intention to adopt (4.50/5.0) and support for construction-phase prosumerism (4.45/5.0). Barriers including skills deficits, institutional fragmentation, and high capital costs, are transitional and addressable through training, coordination, and procurement reform. Overall, the study contributes a transferable spatial method for RE-informed compound siting, extends prosumer theory to temporary project-based infrastructure, and supports low-carbon construction in Sub-Saharan Africa and comparable contexts.

title: Editorial Board
Flexibility-supported optimal scheduling for integrated energy systems under extreme typhoon disasters
Harnessing multiple home-microgrids as cloud energy storage for resource compensation: A comprehensive review
Prospects and challenges: Can co-production of natural gas hydrate with shallow and deep gas achieve “1 + 1 + 1 > 3” in marine gas exploitation?
High-efficiency GaSb thermophotovoltaic cell demonstrated on a planar heat source up to 1800 K for high-temperature applications
Hypercube: A hybrid physics-learning framework for rapid, robust urban building energy modeling
Comprehensive thermal runaway risk assessment of EVs in urban driving: A multi-source information fusion framework based on Bayesian network and modified multiscale sample entropy
A dual-diffusion model for hydrogel-based photovoltaic cooling: Climatic adaptability and national application potential
Economic valuation of battery storage integration in operational solar plants under price uncertainty: a compound real options approach
abstract: Variable renewable energy expansion has intensified the need for battery energy storage systems (BESS) to manage price volatility and operational intermittency in power systems. This work evaluates integrating BESS into operational utility-scale solar plants, focusing on how managerial flexibility mitigates financial risks from price uncertainty. The objective is to develop a decision-making framework to identify the optimal timing and strategy for BESS investment by evaluating different investment paths to maximize project value through energy arbitrage. The methodology employs K-means clustering for price pattern identification and Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) for joint PV-BESS dispatch optimization. These inputs feed a Real Options Analysis (ROA) model using the Least Squares Monte Carlo (LSM) algorithm adapted to compound options, which incorporates stochastic evolution in day and night prices through geometric Brownian motions. Results show the flexible approach yields an expected incremental value of 13.2 MMUSD, reversing the -59.1 MMUSD loss suggested by traditional valuation. The model justifies investment in 83.4% of scenarios, with 53.4% favouring compound expansion over single-stage investment. Furthermore, nighttime price growth and volatility are identified as the most critical drivers of project profitability. This framework serves as a strategic tool for private investors to mitigate declining daytime revenues by transforming static solar assets into flexible systems. Practically, developers should prioritize modular designs and negotiate Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) that capitalize on nighttime price spreads to ensure financial resilience in uncertain market environments.

title: Aligning system flexibility needs and interprovincial coordination for China’s net-zero power transition
Quantifying distributed PV orientation smoothing effects and their impact on electricity grid performance
Uncertainty-aware anomaly detection for wind turbines using a physics-informed spatiotemporal feature modelling model
abstract: Wind turbines are prone to failures in critical subsystems such as the drivetrain and generator, making reliable early anomaly detection essential for safe and stable operation. With the increasing availability of monitored time-series data, data driven methods have emerged as an effective basis for anomaly detection and have demonstrated considerable potential for improving the reliability and safety of wind turbines. Nevertheless, conventional data driven approaches often struggle to adequately characterize the temporal dependencies in wind turbine operational data, the correlations among monitored variables in the feature space, and the physical constraints governing system operation, resulting in limited detection accuracy and robustness under varying operating conditions. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a physics-informed deep learning framework based on multi-sensor data, which integrates spatiotemporal feature modeling with physical consistency to improve the reliability of early anomaly detection and support prognostic functionality for wind turbines. The proposed framework is validated using a real SCADA dataset collected from two wind farms. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed PITG achieves the best predictive performance across four datasets, with an average RMSE of 0.1397 and an average R 2 of 97.21%. Meanwhile, the physics-informed embedding module effectively reduces prediction uncertainty, decreasing the maximum prediction variance by approximately 27.25% compared with the baseline model. Combined with the inverse-variance multi-sensor fusion strategy, the proposed framework achieves an F1-score of 0.566 for system-level anomaly detection, validating its effectiveness and robustness under complex operating conditions.

title: An efficient analytical model for stress-induced capacity fade in pouch lithium-ion batteries
Revealing the coupling mechanism between reaction uniformity and electrochemical performance in redox flow batteries
Resilient energy management in hydrogen-integrated microgrids using actor-critic reinforcement learning
abstract: This paper addresses operational resilience in hydrogen-integrated microgrids, where deep reinforcement learning (DRL) controllers may violate physical constraints under uncertainty. A physics-embedded Actor–Critic Proximal Policy Optimization (AC-PPO) architecture is proposed, in which feasibility-aware action generation and structural constraint embedding are combined with Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) state processing to capture slow hydrogen dynamics and short-horizon prediction. The controller is first evaluated on in-distribution stress scenarios up to 150% load and 60% renewable availability, which represent the upper bound of the designed operating envelope rather than genuine out-of-distribution conditions. Within this envelope, AC-PPO records zero blackout events in the severe-stress case, achieves the lowest operating cost among the compared controllers, and maintains the highest frequency stability. A focused reward-weight sensitivity study further shows that the adopted safety-critical coefficients lie in a stable and interpretable operating region, while separate out-of-distribution tests with load factors up to 2.0, renewable availability down to 0.2, and component-failure scenarios confirm graceful degradation beyond the training envelope. External-data validation using archived Austin weather forcing and a normalized public building-load profile derived from the Dryad dataset further preserves close agreement with the paper baseline, with the reported continuous metrics remaining within 15% of the baseline values and blackout events remaining near zero. Finally, the reported hydrogen metric is clarified as a utilization index rather than thermodynamic round-trip efficiency. These results strengthen the practical credibility of physics-embedded deep reinforcement learning for safety-critical hydrogen-microgrid energy management while also highlighting the remaining need for future hardware-in-the-loop validation.

title: Residential load aggregation for secondary frequency regulation: A privacy-preserving online learning-based approach
Multi-criteria decision analysis of ammonia-based marine power systems for ships
abstract: Ammonia is increasingly regarded as a promising zero‑carbon marine fuel, yet prior studies have assessed its technical, environmental, and economic performance largely in isolation, without integrating operational optimisation, regulatory compliance, and stakeholder-differentiated economic risk within a unified framework, limiting their practical relevance for investment decisions. This study addresses this gap by presenting an integrated multi-criteria assessment of ammonia-based marine power configurations, combining diesel and ammonia dual-fuel generators with fuel cells for a cruise ship operating on two representative routes. A genetic algorithm-based optimisation identifies fuel cell sizing that balances ammonia consumption with onboard operational constraints. The optimised configurations are subsequently evaluated through a multi-criteria decision analysis framework considering well-to-wake emissions, FuelEU and IMO Net-Zero Framework compliance, and lifecycle costs including regulatory penalties across five stakeholder weighting scenarios. A two-stage sensitivity and uncertainty analysis, combining deterministic and Monte Carlo simulation, further quantifies the robustness of the economic results. The results show that integrating ammonia dual-fuel engines with fuel cells achieves net electrical efficiencies of 47–51%, reducing well-to-wake emissions by 83–84% relative to the diesel baseline. The diesel benchmark system incurs the highest annual cost due to regulatory penalties, while ammonia price, rather than capital cost, is the dominant source of economic uncertainty for ammonia-based configurations. Diesel-hybrid fuel cell configurations are the most cost-robust under current uncertainty, whereas full-ammonia fuel cell configurations are projected to achieve superior economic performance as green ammonia costs decline, offering complementary near- and long-term decision pathways for maritime stakeholders.

title: Between energy security and sustainable energy development: quantitative identification of transformational tensions and strategic equilibrium points in the ESSTM model based on the example of European Union countries
abstract: The energy transition is a multidimensional process that includes, among other things, the pursuit of economic decarbonization, energy security, energy affordability, and improved energy efficiency. Achieving these objectives requires reconciling often competing priorities, since progress in one area may weaken or delay actions in another. This means that the energy transition should be assessed as a system of interdependencies, tensions, and trade-offs between the key dimensions of energy system development. In response to this need, the Energy Security–Sustainability Trade-off Matrix (ESSTM) method is proposed as a new quantitative approach for identifying transformation tensions and strategic equilibrium points in the energy systems of the EU-27. The method was applied to assess changes between 2014 and 2023, making it possible to capture both the level of advancement of the transition and shifts in the relationships between its key dimensions. The analysis was based on 19 indicators grouped into five pillars: decarbonization and transformation of the energy structure, energy efficiency and energy management, energy security and system resilience, energy justice and energy affordability, and innovation and infrastructure modernization. The results indicate that the EU energy transition is characterized by growing structural asymmetries. The strongest tensions occur between decarbonization and energy security, between energy security and energy justice, and between decarbonization and energy justice. The study also identifies the “transformation tension paradox,” according to which progress in selected pillars may coexist with a decline in the overall quality of the energy system if systemic tensions increase at the same time. Austria in 2014 and Denmark in 2023 were identified as strategic equilibrium points, while Denmark, Sweden, Finland, and Austria belonged to the most favorable transformation configurations determined on the basis of the Pareto frontier. The results indicate that ESSTM can support decision-makers in monitoring systemic tensions, identifying key trade-offs, and designing more coherent energy and climate policies. It also supports the diagnosis of potential structural tensions that may weaken the coherence and stability of the energy transition process.

title: Energy storage meets intelligence: Towards AI-driven energy management, system design and smart operation with energy-usage awareness
abstract: The energy transition towards deep decarbonisation is urgent, and energy storage has become essential for enabling high penetrations of renewable energy within modern energy systems. Among the available technologies, thermomechanical energy storage (TMES) has attracted growing interest due to its suitability for large-scale and medium/long-duration applications, low environmental impact, long operational lifetime, and strong potential for integration with diverse energy technologies for multi-energy management. At the same time, artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a major driver of innovation in the energy sector, offering new opportunities to enhance system efficiency and operational flexibility across multiple scales. The integration of AI with TMES therefore represents a promising pathway to accelerate deployment, improve performance and enable more adaptive and intelligent operation. In this paper, we review the status of AI-enabled TMES, highlighting its potential roles and synergistic benefits across three key domains: energy management, system design and smart operation. Importantly, we also emphasise the energy-usage awareness associated with application of AI. As data centres continue to expand rapidly to support growing AI workloads, the net energy and carbon benefits of AI-driven solutions in the energy sector become increasingly uncertain if their own energy consumption is not explicitly considered. Building on this analysis, principal challenges and opportunities for AI-driven innovation in TMES and outline future research directions are identified, along with practical pathways for developing energy-aware, intelligent storage systems that can meaningfully contribute to net-zero energy transitions.

title: A novel V2X-enabled co-optimization method for energy management and motion control of hybrid mining trucks
Evaluating pumped hydro storage system impacts through life cycle assessment
abstract: In recent years, the rapid integration of renewable energies like solar and wind introduces grid stability challenges due to their weather-dependent output, making reliable storage solutions such as Pumped Hydro Storage (PHS) systems essential. Consequently, this study aims to evaluate the environmental impacts using Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) methodology. The inventory data stem from simulated energy and water flows through a mathematical-physics model based on Python, referring on an existing European Alpine facility. From an eco-design standpoint, the simulation facilitated preliminary modelling of system flows, enabling detailed analysis of their prediction. Three realistic scenarios were analyzed, featuring energy mixes from wind, grid, hydroelectric plants (HPP), PHS, and demand loads, differentiated by active system elements. The system boundaries adopted for the LCA study are cradle-to-grave, and the impact assessment methods used are ReCiPe 2016 and EF 3.1. The results reveal that the presence of PHS system significantly reduces greenhouse gas emissions (i.e., -81%) and other environmental impacts compared to the baseline scenario (i.e., without PHS), although it introduces environmental burdens primarily associated with steel and cement production for infrastructure construction. This study emphasizes the necessity of enhancing Life Cycle Inventory data quality through primary industry sources and recommends incorporating photovoltaic systems into future models for a more holistic evaluation.

title: Spatiotemporal decoupled coordinated planning for zero-carbon industrial parks
Predictive energy management strategy for fuel cell vehicles to mitigate the adverse effects of cumulative and propagated vehicle speed prediction errors
A radiative-state guided debiasing transformer for patch-wise day-ahead photovoltaic power forecasting
A hybrid prediction model for blast furnace gas generation under diverse operating conditions via multi-feature fusion clustering
Decarbonising cement production through electrification and thermal storage: impacts on electricity markets and transmission redispatch
abstract: Electrification is increasingly considered a key pathway for reducing emissions from cement production, but it shifts clinker heat supply towards greater dependence on power markets and electricity infrastructure. The effects of clinker electrification on day-ahead prices, balancing market participation, and redispatch remain insufficiently understood, although they are important for investment and operation. This study analyses how alternative electrification routes and high-temperature thermal storage at eight German cement plants with plausible reinvestment decisions by 2035 affect day-ahead prices, aFRR capacity provision, and redispatch in Germany. Cement production is represented through fully electrified clinker heat supply, a hydrogen kiln with on-site electrolysis, and partial electrification, benchmarked against a fossil reference. An agent-based model clears the day-ahead market and an aFRR capacity market sequentially. The resulting schedules are checked against transmission constraints and corrected through least-cost redispatch. Electrification raises the volume-weighted average accepted day-ahead price from 21.3 €/MWh in the fossil case to around 25–27 €/MWh. Cement plants contribute mainly to positive aFRR capacity at around 3.7–4.2%, while remaining below 1% in negative aFRR. Peak loading rises near large plants, yet redispatch volume falls from 379.0 TWh to about 360–367 TWh and average redispatch cost declines from about 245 €/MWh to around 140–150 €/MWh. Renewable curtailment decreases from 232.1 TWh to about 227–230 TWh. With thermal storage, cement plants can shift electricity demand, but the grid effect depends on plant location and operating conditions. Across the year, electrification lowers redispatch and renewable curtailment, although some transmission lines are more heavily loaded during severe hours. Plant operation should therefore consider both electricity prices and local grid conditions.

title: Fuelling sustainable aviation: Techno-economic perspectives and airfare implications for methanol-to-jet eSAF under EU regulation
abstract: Achieving net-zero emissions by mid-century demands transformative decarbonisation and defossilisation efforts across the policy, infrastructure, and technological landscape of the European Union. As the EU accelerates the deployment of Sustainable Aviation Fuels (SAF) through the ReFuelEU mandate, targeting a 70% SAF blend by 2050, electrofuels (eSAF) emerge as a central mitigation option for the aviation sector. This study presents a system-level techno-economic perspective on the Methanol-to-Jet (MtJ) route for the production of jet-range hydrocarbons, examined in the Danish context as a strategic case. By combining projections for aviation fuel demand with production cost drivers, the analysis explores a set of scenarios spanning alternative renewable buildout pathways and CO2 procurement cost evolutions. Regulatory impacts are assessed by embedding the scenario analysis in the European policy framework, including potential future alternative support-factor schemes that address the eSAF to conventional fuel cost gap. Finally, fuel cost trajectories are propagated into direct consumer airfare impacts for representative domestic and intra-EEA routes under the mandated blending requirements. Findings show that while eSAF does not achieve cost convergence with conventional jet fuel through technological learning alone, future jet fuel blend cost dynamics are primarily driven by the combined effects of policy design and the increasing economic weight of carbon emissions. From a consumer perspective, compliance with aviation decarbonisation targets results in observable airfare premiums, which range from near price parity to increases of up to approximately 23% by 2030 and up to about 34% by 2050 across the analysed scenarios. Nevertheless, a sustainable transition for aviation hinges not on short-term cost parity, but on timely policy interventions that manage cost pass-throughs, sustain investor confidence, and enable the large-scale deployment of alternative aviation fuels.

title: Online neural fusion of deep reinforcement learning and model predictive control for comfort-aware greenhouse energy optimization
Hidden risk: How pre-existing mechanical defects worsen battery safety under slight overcharge
Hierarchical differentiated customer directrix load-based demand response mechanism for large-scale heterogeneous customers
Electricity procurement and temporal matching for wind-based hydrogen: multi-year optimization and stochastic analysis of levelized cost under market and weather uncertainty
abstract: Abstsract This study develops a stochastic, multi-year optimization framework to evaluate the levelized cost of hydrogen (LCoH) under alternative electricity procurement strategies for wind-based electrolysis in Germany. Using 100 stochastic wind and electricity price scenarios over a 20-year horizon, the model jointly optimizes electrolyzer sizing and dispatch across merchant, co-located, and contract-based configurations, including physical power purchase agreements (PPAs), virtual PPAs, and collar mechanisms. The results show that electricity procurement strategy and temporal matching requirements are the primary determinants of both the level and variability of LCoH. Across most configurations, LCoH ranges between approximately 7.0–9.0 €/kg, while strict temporal matching constraints increase costs to 10.3–12.0 €/kg by reducing operational flexibility and requiring substantial electrolyzer oversizing. In contrast, unconstrained merchant operation achieves a mean LCoH of 6.97 €/kg, illustrating the economic significance of renewable matching requirements. Co-located systems benefit from electricity market participation and export revenues, although their competitiveness depends strongly on captured electricity prices. Physical and virtual PPAs yield similar cost outcomes at equivalent strike prices, indicating that contract price is more influential than contract form under the modeled assumptions. Collar mechanisms provide an intermediate solution by balancing expected cost and variability through bounded price exposure. The results further reveal a structural trade-off between renewable project bankability and hydrogen cost competitiveness, driven by the interaction between strike prices, hedge volumes, and capture prices. Overall, the results demonstrate that regulation, procurement design, and market structure are as influential as technological progress in determining renewable hydrogen competitiveness.

title: A cross-domain degradation mode prediction of lithium iron phosphate batteries for full cycle life
On the climatic and energy impacts of reflective and evaporative photovoltaic roofs in cities
Two-stage coordinated robust electricity trading for virtual power plants across the annual-to-spot trading cycle under asynchronous wholesale-retail interaction
Reimagining energy transitions: understanding energy autonomy through community participation and epistemic cultures in marginalised Indian communities
A dual-function energy regenerative suspension supported AIoT for energy harvesting and self-sensing to enhance the performance of fuel-powered and battery electric vehicles
Uncertainty self-balancing capability: A novel indicator for microgrid flexibility and its economic valuation
Influence of linear, mixed-integer linear, piecewise-linear, and nonlinear thermal power flow models on district heating network design
abstract: Optimization enables cost-effective district heating network design, but scalability constraints limit its applicability to large urban districts. Although many mixed-integer linear programming models rely on linearized thermal power flow models, no study has systematically investigated how regression model choices affect computational scalability and network design quality. Existing benchmarks compare entire optimization frameworks without isolating the impact of the underlying thermal flow model, since the chosen regression directly determines the achievable district size and the design reliability. Thus, this paper systematically compares six regression models for pipe investment costs and heat losses. Piecewise-linear regressions achieve the highest accuracy for investment costs, while logarithmic models achieve the highest accuracy for heat losses. Seven linear, mixed-integer linear, and nonlinear programming formulations based on these regressions are benchmarked across 56 real-world districts with up to 10,000 heat sinks, spanning forced and economic designs, single and multiple design periods, and single and multiple heat sources. A novel hybrid thermal power flow model is introduced, and a nonlinear power flow model incorporating economic connection decisions for heat sinks is implemented. Results reveal that purely linear models offer the shortest solving times but usually yield inferior network designs. Piecewise-linear models achieve the best objective values yet suffer from limited scalability for districts. Affine and hybrid models deliver near-optimal solutions with significantly improved scalability, while constant models sacrifice minimal optimality for substantial gains in solvable district size. For multi-period and economic optimizations, only linear formulations achieve optimal designs for large districts with more than 2250 heat sinks, whereas hybrid and constant models best balance solution quality and computational efficiency for medium-scale systems.

title: Evaluating isothermal degradation error in lithium-ion batteries under WLTP drive cycles
abstract: Physics-based battery management systems frequently assume isothermal cell oper-ation, eliminating the thermal sub-model to reduce computational cost. The error introduced by this assumption in state-of-health prediction depends on the activation energy of the solid electrolyte interphase kinetic rate constant. In widely used pa-rameterisations this energy is set to zero, decoupling temperature from degradation kinetics and concealing the true thermal sensitivity. A calibrated multi-mechanism Single Particle Model with Electrolyte is developed for nickel manganese cobalt oxide and lithium iron phosphate cells. A two-stage sequential procedure calibrates the ac-tivation energy from temperature-dependent fade rate ratios, then jointly optimises the solid electrolyte interphase rate constant and loss of active material coefficient against a longitudinal state-of-health trajectory, achieving a root mean square er-ror of 1 . 45 pp. — 6 . 3-fold improvement over the uncalibrated default. A parametric sweep of 24 conditions spanning both chemistries, ambient temperatures of 10, 25, and 40 °C, and charge rates of 1C and 2C shows that the isothermal assumption in-troduces state-of-health errors of 1 . 4–8 . 2 pp. (for nickel manganese cobalt oxide) over 500 Worldwide Harmonised Light Vehicle Test Procedure cycles with the calibrated activation energy of 78 . 5 kJ mol −1 , compared with a maximum of 0 . 20 pp. at zero ac-tivation energy. For nickel manganese cobalt oxide cells, solid electrolyte interphase growth accounts for >99% of capacity loss. For lithium iron phosphate cells, solid electrolyte interphase and loss of active material contribute approximately 62% and 38% respectively, due to the larger depth of discharge per cycle. A three-layer parameter uncertainty analysis one-at-a-time sensitivity, an activation energy sweep across 62 – 95 kJ mol −1 , and an analytical Monte Carlo, confirms that the isothermal Δ SOH error exceeds 0.5 pp. across the full physically plausible parameter space and that activation energy is the dominant source of uncertainty.

title: Techno-economic optimization of reversible solid oxide cell systems under price fluctuations considering multi-period dynamics and physical and chemical degradation
Future role of heavy-duty fuel cell vehicles in the decarbonization of the freight transport
abstract: As the world shifts towards cleaner and more sustainable transportation solutions, understanding the requirements and implications of hydrogen fuel cell technology in heavy-duty vehicles is crucial for informing industry developments and policy decisions. The objective of this paper is to investigate the hydrogen consumption and powertrain efficiency of heavy-duty fuel cell vehicles (HDFCVs) in various vehicle segments and powertrain designs. To achieve this, a comprehensive methodology was employed, involving the integration of reference HDFCV models into the VECTO platform, simulation of different powertrain architectures using MATLAB Simulink, and estimation of current and future hydrogen demand for the heavy-duty vehicle fleet. The key results of this study indicate that the design spaces presented can serve as a baseline for industry stakeholders to select optimal battery sizes, fuel cell system powers, and hydrogen tank sizes, thereby accelerating vehicle development. Furthermore, policymakers can utilize the data on hydrogen consumption and powertrain efficiency to define key performance indicators, estimate future hydrogen demands, and compare the environmental impact of HDFCVs with other propulsion systems. In terms of HDFCV fleet H 2 demand, addressing all the uncertainties raised in this work, it may vary from 1.6 to 2.8 Mt of H 2 yearly, implying up to 3% of the current H 2 production. Therefore, the H 2 production infrastructure is able to accommodate more ambitious H 2 -related scenarios for the HDV sector. Finally, the H 2 consumption ranges per vehicle class and powertrain design, together with the H 2 tank capacity values sized on the basis of official VECTO cycles, constitute an original reference dataset—grounded in a mathematically guaranteed minimum consumption via an optimal energy management strategy—that can be directly used by vehicle manufacturers as a baseline for preliminary powertrain and hydrogen storage system design.

title: Lifecycle assessment and optimization of integrated blue-green hydrogen production and liquefaction with reforming-electrolysis coupling
Energy storage under extreme conditions: challenges and strategies for MXene-based supercapacitors
Frequency-coordinated conditional diffusion model for extreme-value-aware wind power forecasting
Dual-stream time-frequency multi-task learning for weak disturbance event identification and localisation in power distribution networks
abstract: The accurate identification and localisation of disturbance events are critical to ensuring the reliability and safety of power distribution networks. However, existing techniques may encounter difficulties with weak transient events such as High Impedance Faults (HIFs) and switching operations. Motivated by recent advancements in Synchro-Waveform measurements, this paper develops a waveform-based data-driven method for distribution network event diagnosis. A novel data-driven framework built upon the Dual-Stream Time-Frequency Fusion Network with Multi-task Learning (DSTFF-MTL) is proposed. It is designed to capture decoupled temporal, spatial and frequency-domain features embedded in the measured waveforms. Temporal and spatial features are extracted through cascaded ModernTCN models in one stream, whereas global frequency patterns are learned through a complex-valued frequency network in the other. These two streams are fused using an Interlaced Attentional Feature Fusion Network (IAFF), and the resulting features are processed by a conflict-aware multi-task classifier to jointly predict event type and location. Furthermore, a Selective Fine-tuning (SFT) strategy is developed to enable few-shot adaptation under topology reconfiguration, renewable integration, and neutral grounding changes. Validation on the IEEE 33-bus network demonstrates that DSTFF-MTL improves M-F1 by 4% for event identification and 15% for localisation over baseline methods under the same training settings. Validation on the IEEE 123-bus network demonstrates scalability to larger distribution systems. On a real-world waveform dataset, the model achieves 95.8% accuracy. Additional experiments confirm its computational efficiency, requiring only 6.8 ms to process each 100 ms sample, and its robustness against noise, harmonics, measurement anomalies, and line parameter variations.

title: In-operando detection of lithium plating during fast charging via anode dynamic electrochemical impedance spectroscopy in lithium-ion batteries
Real-time implementation of a synergistic HEMS framework: Integrating meta-heuristic demand side management and CVR-based voltage control for enhanced residential energy efficiency
A bi-level resilience-oriented planning framework for hydrogen-integrated multi-energy systems under extreme events
Co-optimization of storage service scheduling and bidding strategies for community-shared energy storage: a distributionally robust bi-level model
Recent advances in photocatalytic fragmentation and upgradation of lignin to high-value products using engineered metal sulphide photocatalysts
abstract: Photocatalytic cleavage of C β -O bonds in lignin to aromatic monomers and upgradation of generated aromatic monomers to high-value C-C coupled products are promising strategies to replace the utilization of fossil resources in the production of carbon-based compounds. Metal sulphide photocatalysts have shown great potential in enhancing both the converting lignin and the upgrading lignin-derived aromatic monomers, owing to their superior photophysical properties, such as abundant active sites, prolonged charge carrier lifetimes, and tuneable band structures with appropriate photoredox capabilities. This review summarizes recent advances in the design and modification of metal sulphides to improve several key steps in lignocellulosic valorisation, including enhancing C α -H bond activation or C α -OH group oxidation in lignin to facilitate C β -O bond cleavage, promoting hydrogen transfer efficiency for the formation of aromatic monomers, selectively activating C α -H or O-H bonds in lignin-derived compounds to generate different C-C coupled products, and facilitating the activation of C=O bonds in lignin-derived ketones to generate C-C coupled products. Current challenges and future perspectives for the development of metal sulphide-based systems in photocatalytic lignin valorisation are also discussed.

title: High-resolution simulation and modeling of tropical-cyclone induced power outages in the United States
abstract: Storm driven power outages impose large and uneven costs on communities, yet operational outage prediction models remain constrained by available datasets. Existing approaches either provide high resolution forecasts for a small number of utilities with internal outage records, or operate across broad regions with insufficient resolution for local planning. We address this gap by first assembling a new sub-kilometer scale multi-utility outage dataset that combines scraped outage records across nine states and ten utility service territories with county-level customers affected data. Based on this new dataset we then develop a topologically informed statistical framework to estimate outage rates and the number of customers affected based on gridded wind, precipitation, and storm surge fields, distribution line exposure, undergrounding, and social vulnerability characteristics. On held-out storms, the framework outperformed existing outage models for the contiguous United States (CONUS). Using the trained model, we reconstruct a decade of tropical cyclone driven outages for 53 events on a uniform high resolution sub-kilometer scale grid. Analyses of this dataset reveal that counties with higher social vulnerability suffer systematically higher outage rates compared to less vulnerable counties exposed to similar wind speeds, partially because counties with the highest levels of social vulnerability are most likely to have high levels of overhead exposure compared to the least vulnerable communities.

title: Distributed flexible dispatch of heterogeneous thermostatically controlled loads with physically consistent neural ODEs
abstract: Thermostatically controlled loads (TCLs) are the major energy sources in buildings that provide flexible load adjustment in power systems. The flexible dispatch of TCLs requires modeling thermal dynamics to measure indoor temperature variations and optimizing power consumption to provide flexibility to power grids while satisfying occupant comfort preferences. However, when dispatching TCLs across multiple buildings, heterogeneous building structures and comfort preferences can lead to different model complexities in thermal dynamics and temperature regulation intervals, both of which can make traditional methods insufficient or even infeasible for problem-solving. To tackle this challenge, this work first develops a novel Physically Consistent Neural Ordinary Differential Equation (PC-NODE) model to represent thermal dynamics, integrating weight learning and physics-informed loss functions to ensure a unified model structure and physics consistency. The developed continuous model is then seamlessly transformed into discrete equation constraints to represent comfort preferences with different time intervals. Furthermore, an asynchronous Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM)-based distributed optimization method is proposed to coordinate buildings with heterogeneous comfort preferences by differentiating the frequency of local variable updates across buildings based on the time interval. Simulation results for a 12-building dispatch case demonstrate that the single-zone model trained by PC-NODE significantly improves statistical accuracy, whereas asynchronous ADMM achieves near-optimal economic performance relative to ground-truth centralized optimization.

title: Multi-objective dynamic reconfiguration of active distribution networks via spatio-temporal flexible interaction of SOPs and ESSs against critical DG disconnections
Research on the technical potential and complementary development pattern of offshore wind and photovoltaics in China's coastal regions under climate change
Electrolyte-mediated interfacial engineering for silicon-based anodes in lithium-ion batteries: From liquid to quasi-solid and all-solid-state systems
Coordinating electricity and computility in economic dispatch by embedding quantile convex latency surrogates
Hydrogen-driven co-optimization of production and energy systems for low-carbon steel industrial parks
Delivering building demand flexibility for grid-interactive operation: from perception and cognition to decision, execution, and verification
abstract: As both buildings and power systems undergo rapid decarbonization, demand flexibility (DF) in buildings has emerged as a key enabler for renewable energy integration, grid reliability, energy resilience, and efficient and low carbon operation. By dynamically adjusting building energy use in response to grid requirements, DF can help reduce building operational costs, respond to renewable variability, reduce peak demand, alleviate network congestion, and enhance overall system stability. Consequently, significant research efforts have examined building DF from multiple perspectives, including flexibility definitions, resources, characterization, assessment, optimization, and application scenarios. However, the effective delivery of DF in buildings requires an integrated, end-to-end approach spanning perception, cognition, decision, execution, and verification, which remains a critical gap in the existing literature. This review addresses this gap by proposing a layered architecture that integrates these stages into a coherent framework and provides insights from existing studies in this field. It synthesizes enabling methods, clarifies cross-layer interactions, and examines how data, models, control strategies, implementation mechanisms, and evaluation approaches collectively support DF delivery. Critical cross-layer challenges are identified, and future research priorities for robust and trustworthy DF delivery are outlined. This work establishes a conceptual foundation for advancing interoperable, grid-responsive, and practically deployable DF solutions in buildings, supporting both building decarbonization and more efficient, resilient grid operation

title: AI-driven smart home appliance optimization: A systematic review
Climate-responsive roof cooling strategies for low-energy carbon-neutral buildings: A nationwide comparative assessment of radiative sky cooling and green roofs
Physical-economic-health coordination for hydrogen-electrified ship power systems: A triple-layer unified framework
Ms-MOARO: a novel multi-strategy optimizer for multi-objective optimal power flow with wind-solar-tidal energy integration
Robust design of multi-energy systems accounting for mixed-integer operational problems
abstract: Identifying robust designs for multi-energy systems is computationally challenging. As rigorous approaches are often computationally intractable, heuristics are employed to generate candidate designs. Specifically, we consider a heuristic that iteratively identifies and adds extreme scenarios to the design problem. We theoretically investigate how three common nonconvexities, i.e., piecewise-linear energy inflow-outflow relationships, minimum part-loads, and storage complementarity, affect the robustness of designs identified by this heuristic. We find that, if surplus energy cannot be curtailed, any of these nonconvexities may cause the heuristic to fail. If curtailment is allowed, storage complementarity does not compromise robustness, and convex piecewise-linear inflow-outflow relationships can be reformulated linearly. However, minimum part-loads may lead to the failure of the heuristic. Furthermore, if the optimal value function of the operational problem is nonconvex in the uncertain variables, the heuristic may fail. We demonstrate these findings using an illustrative multi-energy system case study, in which minimum part-loads and nonconvex dependence of the objective function on heat-pump efficiency are identified as possible failure modes. We rigorously verify the robustness of a design identified using the heuristic and find a scenario where, in one time step, 1.1 kW of the 313.6 kW electricity demand could not be satisfied. However, when the number of representative scenarios is increased from 4 to 6 or 8 , the resulting designs are robust. This demonstrates that the heuristic can serve as an effective first step in identifying robust designs. However, when robustness guarantees are required, a rigorous solution method must be employed.
